Gianni Infantino has made a new funding pledge to Fifa members in the fallout of his botched World Cup sell-off scheme.

A letter seen by various publications was sent out to the six continental confederations on Monday, in which Infantino suggested more money could be distributed to national associations from its reserves.

This followed calls from Uefa and Concacaf for a $2.1bn payout from the world football governing body, along with an independent review of Fifa’s reserves after Infantino tried to sell stakes in competitions including the World Cup to private investors under the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered", with the proposal to be considered on 15 October when the Fifa Council meet.

"I will not prejudge the amount," Infantino said in the letter.

"A single figure can begin the discussion, but it cannot complete a global policy."

Infantino added that any funding would be subject to financial checks and formal approval amid scrutiny of his governance.

"Until the assessment and necessary approvals are complete, no preliminary figure can be treated as an approved commitment to the Member Associations," he wrote.

Gianni Infantino has made a fresh funding pledge to Fifa members ( Reuters )

The Swiss-Italian also launched his latest defence of the failed FFE plan which has resulted in calls for his resignation, reiterating his intention was to generate additional income for the good of the game.

He had given member associations an ultimatum in regards to potential funding, telling federation heads that they could miss out on $30m if they did not back his scheme.

"The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable Fifa to invest more in football not to replace support that could responsibly be provided from existing resources," he added. "So, it would actually have been on top of it."

Infantino is vying for re-election as Fifa president despite the torrent of criticism that has come his way, with the election to be held in March 2027.

Additional reporting from Reuters

Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott has been jailed for seven years for sexually abusing children.

The 49-year-old subjected a girl and a boy, who were both of primary school age at the time, to multiple incidents of abuse.

He targeted the girl between 1993 and 1996 and the boy between 2006 and 2010.

Dott appeared at the High Court in Edinburgh on Tuesday, where judge Lord Harrower told him he had “robbed the complainers of a significant part of their childhood”.

Imposing a backdated sentence of seven years, he said that Dott’s behaviour had involved a “gross violation of trust”.

open image in gallery Graeme Dott was sentenced to seven years in prison ( PA Wire )

Dott was earlier found guilty of two counts of lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour towards children following a five-day trial at the same court in August.

During the trial, jurors heard that he exposed himself in front of both children, touched them inappropriately, and kissed them.

In the cases of both victims, the abuse happened in the Glasgow area.

Dott had denied the charges but was found guilty.

open image in gallery Dott, pictured during the World Snooker Championship at the Crucible Theatre in 2013 ( Getty )

Lord Harrower remanded him in custody and his name was added to the sex offenders register.

Dott, who turned professional in 1994, won the World Snooker Championship in 2006, defeating Peter Ebdon in the final at the Crucible in Sheffield.

He reached the final in two other years but was beaten by Ronnie O’Sullivan in 2004 and Neil Robertson in 2010.

Following his conviction, Dott’s name was removed from World Snooker’s Hall of Fame.

If you are a child and you need help because something has happened to you, you can call Childline free of charge on 0800 1111. You can also call the NSPCC if you are an adult and you are worried about a child, on 0808 800 5000. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adults on 0808 801 0331.

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has revealed his side remain uncertain about how they will approach Sunday’s ‘home’ behind-closed-doors Nations League fixture with Israel in Serbia.

A majority of players, described as “significant” by the Football Association of Ireland, ultimately elected to fulfil their ‘away’ clash in Debrecen, Hungary, a contest that was swirling in a debate that shows little sign of abating before Thursday’s meeting with Austria at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

On Saturday, FAI president Paul Cooke reaffirmed their intention was to play Israel again in Backa Topola, but said his organisation was taking things “one game at a time”.

Hallgrimsson, also speaking after the 3-0 triumph in Hungary, said of the situation: “We haven’t decided what we will do 100 per cent. When we get home tonight, we’ll give them a day off tomorrow to go home, and share a day with their families and friends and loved ones, and then we’ll come back and prepare for the Austria game.

open image in gallery Heimir Hallgrimsson is unsure how Ireland will approach another Israel clash ( Reuters )

“Hopefully we can finish that one and take a discussion.”

Gavin Bazunu was the only member of the Republic squad to officially make himself unavailable for selection for the Israel matches, but, as of Saturday, the plan was for the Bolton goalkeeper to remain with the team and be with them for the Austria match.

Asked if it was fair to say there were vastly differing opinions among his men over the Israel tie, Hallgrimsson said: “All I can say is I think we are all uncomfortable, number one.

“Number two, we have different opinions, and we should allow people to have different opinions. It’s not one opinion that’s right and all the others are wrong.

“We have different players in the squad that come from different backgrounds, so we need to be careful that everybody has a say in our decisions. But it’s tough when there are different decisions.

“Just like politics, some parties just can’t work together, but it’s been amazing and I hope you will see the tough times the players have been through and come out as winners, because they want to represent their country.

“That’s their desire. I hope everybody sees that.”

Bazunu came forward on Saturday morning to outline his stance, which he later confirmed in a statement on Instagram. That triggered a lengthy team meeting that resulted in the vote to proceed with the first Israel clash.

Hallgrimsson has repeatedly insisted he and his team have found themselves in a no-win situation. Even after Sunday’s contest – in which players wore black armbands, refused handshakes and bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem – sentiment remains deeply divided over their actions and decisions.

open image in gallery Ireland players bow their head during Israel national anthem ( AP )

The Ireland boss nevertheless does not fear Bazunu will be perceived as “good” or the rest of the players “bad” in Dublin.

“I think both can come out as winners,” he added. “It was obviously a brave decision for Gav to do it. It was tough for us and a lot of players, and we needed to react, but obviously everyone supports Gav and don’t want him to feel bad about what he did.

“It would have been better for me as a coach that the decision came earlier, but when he told me, he explained that overnight he’d changed his mind and didn’t want to play.

“That’s understandable. Nobody forces a player to play for us.”

An attorney who supported President Donald Trump’s false 2020 election claims has resigned from a Justice Department inquiry examining whether former government officials plotted against the Republican president, according to a person familiar with the matter speaking on Monday.

Kurt Olsen’s departure from the so-called "grand conspiracy" investigation marks further upheaval for a meandering probe that has proceeded in fits and starts while prosecutors pursue an ill-defined right-wing theory of a plot against Trump. The development comes just weeks after another Trump ally, Joseph DiGenova, stepped down from leading the closely watched inquiry in Florida.

The person who confirmed Olsen’s resignation spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal personnel matters. Olsen did not immediately reply to an email seeking comment on Monday.

open image in gallery Kurt Olsen, who backed President Donald Trump’s false 2020 election claims has resigned from a Justice Department investigation ( Reuters )

Although Olsen’s prominence as an election denier raised his profile within Trump’s orbit, his lack of prior experience as a Justice Department prosecutor made him an unconventional choice to lead such a high-profile investigation.

Investigators have directed their attention toward multiple major federal inquiries involving Trump, including the probe into Russian interference during the 2016 election and the investigation into his retention of classified records at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida. Prosecutors have demanded testimony from officials connected to both of those prior cases as they search for any evidence of a potential conspiracy intended to deprive Trump of his legal rights.

Olsen’s role in the probe came into sharper focus earlier this month when legal counsel for former CIA Director John Brennan revealed that he had discussed with Olsen a grand jury subpoena compelling Brennan to testify in Fort Pierce on Oct. 25. The attorney, Wainstein, noted that Olsen informed him that Brennan also remains a "target" of a separate, narrower investigation into false statements.

The resignation is the latest sign of instability in the yearlong conspiracy inquiry. Last April, a lead national security prosecutor assigned to the Brennan investigation was replaced after raising questions about the overall strength of the case. Days later, diGenova was sworn in to lead the effort.

open image in gallery Olsen’s prominence as an election denier elevated his profile in the Trump orbit, but his absence of experience as a Justice Department prosecutor made him an unconventional pick for such a high-profile investigation ( Reuters )

The 81-year-old DiGenova previously served as the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia during the Reagan administration and has spent years as a prominent ally of Trump, aiding efforts to overturn the 2020 election outcome and publicly asserting that the president was targeted by an intelligence community conspiracy.

DiGenova resigned earlier this month without filing a single criminal charge. It remains uncertain whether any indictments will ultimately be brought, or what specific information has been gathered to substantiate claims of a government plot against Trump by the officials who investigated him.

Olsen, who unsuccessfully urged the Justice Department in 2020 to back the president’s false election claims, joined the department several months ago after serving in a White House position as director of election security and integrity.

He previously helped Texas Republican attorney general Ken Paxton launch a long-shot attempt to persuade the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn Joe Biden’s 2020 victory, and later represented Kari Lake in her legal attempt to overturn her loss in the 2022 Arizona gubernatorial election. Courts in Arizona eventually sanctioned Olsen for making false statements during that litigation.

A Chinese team has set a Guinness World Record for the most autonomous underwater vehicles operating simultaneously, deploying 116 of the small robots in a swimming pool test.

The trial involved a swarm of drones called TH-618s, the university said in a statement on 24 September.

The test took place on 29 August in a pool measuring 50m by 20m (164ft by 65ft), under the supervision of Guinness World Records officials, who have since certified and published the record.

The record was set by a team from Northwestern Polytechnical University, working with Xian Tianhe Maritime Technologies, a marine equipment and vehicle supplier and a subsidiary of the private defence contractor Xian Tianhe Defence Technology.

The vehicles were deployed in sequence and carried out autonomous underwater formation navigation with no human intervention for 34 minutes over a distance of 500m, following a preset route using real-time data.

"Enabling dozens or even hundreds of underwater vehicles to achieve fully autonomous, long-duration, and stable coordinated navigation in such an environment has always been a core challenge in the global field of underwater intelligent equipment," the university said in its statement.

"This time, the stable navigation of a cluster of hundreds of vehicles represents a breakthrough in the large-scale coordinated navigation of underwater unmanned systems."

The TH-618 vehicles are 61.5cm (24.2in) long and 20cm (7.8in) wide, weigh 5.14kg (11.33lb), and have a maximum range of 30km (18.6 miles) and a battery life of more than eight hours, the university said. They navigate using a mobile phone vision camera system and can adjust their route to correct for disturbances.

China has been rapidly advancing its autonomous vehicle technology, including drone swarms across land, air and sea, as militaries around the world shift away from crewed platforms towards uncrewed systems.

Ukraine said in December that it had carried out the first underwater drone strike on a submarine, hitting a Russian vessel docked in Novorossiysk, a port city on the Black Sea.

In July, researchers from Dalian Maritime University and the China Coast Guard Academy published a proposal for contested islands in the South China Sea to be defended by coordinated drone swarms, including underwater vehicles used to cover detection blind spots.

The paper was published in the Chinese-language journal Command Control & Simulation, which is supervised by the state-run China Shipbuilding Industry Corporation.

Underwater drone swarms have also been tested elsewhere, including a European Union-funded project involving 41 autonomous robots, according to the European Commission.

England legend Lawrence Dallaglio is putting his Rugby World Cup winner’s medal up for sale amid his bankruptcy and ongoing financial troubles.

Dallaglio was a key part of the England squad that won the 2003 World Cup – dramatically beating Australia 20-17 in the final thanks to Jonny Wilkinson’s drop goal in extra time – and has worked as a pundit since his retirement from playing in 2008.

However, the 54-year-old was declared bankrupt last year after racking up hundreds of thousands of pounds of debt to HM Revenue and Customs and others.

Now, he is putting his medal up for auction at Budds in Wellingborough, Northamptonshire, with an estimate of £50,000 to £80,000.

Dallaglio, who won 85 caps for England between 1995 and 2007 while also going on three British and Irish Lions tours, was also part of England’s 2007 World Cup that lost in the final to South Africa – with that runners-up medal being put up for auction as well, with an estimated value of £10,000.

His 2003 Six Nations winner’s medal (£5,000), British and Irish Lions cap (£5,500), England cap (£8,000) and individual awards for two European Cups and three league titles with Wasps (£8,000 each) are also all part of the collection, which could raise as much as £180,000 in total.

open image in gallery Lawrence Dallaglio (left) was a key part of England’s World Cup-winning squad in 2003 ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Dallaglio was part of a strong Wasps contingent in that side ( Getty Images )

Auctioneer Budds said of the World Cup winner’s medal: “It was presented to Dallaglio on November 22, 2003 in Sydney, following victory in the Rugby World Cup final against host nation Australia.

“England defeated Australia 20-17 after extra time. It was the pinnacle of world rugby and the singular greatest achievement in English rugby history.”

In his first major interview since being declared bankrupt last May, which came after his divorce from estranged wife Alice, Dallaglio spoke toThe High Performance podcast and admitted he “could have done things a lot better”.

Dallaglio said: “As a result of getting divorced, I was made bankrupt. I had some financial problems.

“And I probably was guilty of withdrawing back into my little shell and going a little bit into hibernation because, naturally, I’m quite a sort of extrovert, confident, bubbly individual – annoyingly confident sometimes.

“What I didn’t expect was so much of a period of such self-pity. I’ve been a little bit guilty of being a bit sort of, ‘Isn’t life really unkind?’ and ‘Haven’t things worked out against me? Is it all me or is it just bad timing?’”

open image in gallery Dallaglio has worked as a pundit since his retirement ( Getty )

Reflecting on what he could have done differently, Dallaglio added: “Much of it was my own doing. That’s the first thing you have to acknowledge. I could have done things a lot better.

“Might not have got divorced. I could have been one of those people that just parks all the real feelings and just carries on and lives a lie. I don’t know. Maybe I could have carried on doing that.”

Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie’s daughter Zahara Jolie-Pitt is now officially Zahara Jolie after legally dropping her father’s last name.

The 21-year-old will now go by “Zahara Marley Jolie,” according to court documents obtained by The Independent, which show a California judge approved the name change without objection.

The Independent has contacted Pitt’s representatives for comment.

Pitt, 62, and Angelina, 51, share six children: Maddox, 25, Pax, 22, Zahara, 21, Shiloh, 20, and 18-year-old twins Vivienne and Knox. The couple, who met while filming Mr. & Mrs. Smith, began dating in 2005, married in 2014 and separated two years later. Their divorce was finalized in December 2024.

Zahara is now the third of Pitt’s children to legally remove his surname from their’s. She follows in the footsteps of Shiloh, who filed to drop Pitt’s name on her 18th birthday back in 2024 and Maddox, whose name change became official earlier this month.

open image in gallery Zahara Jolie (left), daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, has officially removed “Pitt” from her last name ( Getty )

open image in gallery Pitt and Angelina — who separated in 2016 — share six children, three of whom have now legally dropped their father’s surname ( Getty Images Europe )

Meanwhile, Vivienne filed to change her name from “Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt” to “Vivienne Marcheline Jolie” on her 18th birthday this past July. Her name change petition court hearing is set for November 2.

The name changes come 10 years after an alleged altercation involving Pitt and his family onboard a private jet from France to Los Angeles in 2016, which Jolie previously claimed led to their divorce.

In court documents after she filed for divorce in 2016, Jolie accused Pitt of physical and emotional abuse on board the flight, which Pitt denied. He was later investigated and cleared by multiple agencies. Pitt, meanwhile, has accused his ex-wife of alienating their six children against him, which Jolie has denied.

In 2023, a scathing Father’s Day post, reportedly from Pax’s private Instagram account, emerged in which he said to his adoptive dad: “Happy Father’s Day to this world class a***hole. You time and time and again prove yourself to be a terrible and despicable person.”

When Shiloh filed to change her name in 2024, her lawyer Peter Levine said in a statement shared with People that she had “made an independent and significant decision following painful events.”

Pitt has largely remained tight-lipped about his relationship with his children, rarely addressing the reported estrangement publicly.

However, in a recent interview with Esquire, he revealed he had felt suicidal during “one little period” of his life.

“The pain was so oppressive that – I wasn’t going to act on this, but I could feel – I could feel the cold steel of the bullet in my head, and it felt like relief,” he said.

Asked by the interviewer what sparked his suicidal feelings, Pitt replied: “Family stuff. We could leave it at that.”

Actor Joseph Fiennes, the cousin of Sir Ranulph Fiennes, secretly visited him in a London care home last year while he was living there under an assumed name.

The Shakespeare in Love actor reportedly spent time with the famous explorer before then raising concerns with the authorities about the 82-year-old’s welfare six months later.

The 56-year-old had written to the Office of the Public Guardian on 6 January this year to express concern that Sir Ranulph was being cut off from his loved ones.

The whereabouts of the UK’s most well-known adventurer has been the source of public speculation in recent days, after it was alleged he has been admitted to a number of different care homes under fake names by his wife.

Cheshire Police have said they are aware of the concerns regarding Sir Ranulph, and are satisfied he is living in an appropriate setting with suitable care.

open image in gallery Joseph Fiennes has said the incident has thrown up ‘vital questions’ about care home services and legal services (Ian West/PA) ( PA Wire )

They said there were “no immediate safeguarding concerns”.

Now, The Times has reported that his cousin Joseph visited him at KYN Hurlingham in west London last year, where he had been registered under the name Ron Westwood.

The visit came after his close friends reportedly spent months attempting to visit him, with his first wife Ginny’s sister Arabella Pepper saying his location was only found after friends began telephoning hospitals in an attempt to trace him.

After a staff member at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital allegedly disclosed he had been returned to KYN Hurlingham, Ms Pepper booked herself into the home as a resident and found him there.

Upon finding him, she said Sir Ranulph had appeared “incredibly relieved” and had asked her to deliver a message to his loved ones that he was “longing to see them”.

Later that afternoon, Joseph appeared and spent several minutes “laughing and joking” with Sir Ranulph before they entered a private room to continue their discussion.

The cousins have a close relationship and have appeared in two television documentaries together, including one in which they travelled through Canada together.

open image in gallery The famous explorer has not been seen in two years ( Getty )

On Monday, the actor expressed his concern over Sir Ranulph’s whereabouts, telling The Telegraph: “If that happens to Ran, I can’t bear to think how many others that has happened to and is happening to.

“It throws up vital questions, including questions for care homes and legal services.”

Famous friends of Sir Ranulph, including Bear Grylls, Ben Fogle, Joanna Lumley, John Simpson and Monty Don have spoken out about the situation in recent weeks, with growing calls for an investigation into his wellbeing by both the police and the Office of the Public Guardian.

King Charles was also reportedly blocked from checking on his wellbeing after being alerted to concerns about his declining health and isolation.

Charles was left “most concerned” about his longtime friend, who has not been seen in public for two years, after fellow explorer Anton Bowring wrote to him in February last year asking for his help.

But Sir Ranulph’s wife Louise Millington-Cotes was said to have blocked the King’s attempts to reach out, it has been reported.

Over the weekend, the explorer’s stepson Alexander Millington-Cotes claimed police had ignored his pleas for help and called for an investigation into his whereabouts.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

Sports.title: First Premier League owner breaks silence on Man City guilty verdict as he says it’s no different to an athlete doping
Sports.content:
Next

HULL CITY owner Acun Ilicali has become the first to break silence on Manchester City’s guilty verdict.

The Citizens were found guilty of 114 of their initial 115 charges last week.



Man City have maintained their innocence and are expected to appeal against the verdict.

Ilicali, 57, has become the first owner in the Premier League to speak about the situation.



The Turkish businessman has compared the allegations to an athlete doping in the Olympics.

Speaking on the 1904 Club podcast: “I don’t say they are guilty or not because they are saying they are innocent.



“I think the Premier League says they are not innocent.

“If they are not innocent and they did something.

“I think [it is] not different than having doping and [winning] the Olympic medal.

“This is financial doping at the end of the day. Bringing top four or five players with huge money, breaking the rules.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“From that side, it doesn’t look very positive.”

Ilicali became a Premier League owner this year after helping Hull City gain promotion out of the Championship.

He has been the owner of the club since 2022.

Hull were relegated from the Prem in both 2014/15 and 2016/17 which are both seasons in which City are accused of rule breaks.

Ilicali added: “‘As an owner, I shouldn’t speak too much about it, I think, because I’m not inside it to know everything about it in detail.



“From my side, I will make a general speech, which is if something involved in football is unfair… it should be punished.

“If you give a small punishment, then everybody will do it.

“For the future of football, and a clean future, this kind of thing, if it happens, should be punished and not let people do something like that.

“I like natural money in football. For us, we will not have the budget of the top six or maybe top 10 teams in England, but we respect that.

“We have enough distance because of this income they have naturally.



“Please don’t add more distance. If there is a mistake like this, these kind of mistakes give crazy advantages to some teams and this is not fair.”

Man City chief executive Ferran Soriano has defiantly told European club bosses the Etihad outfit are ready for a long-term fight.

In a meeting of the EFC’s ruling board, including TWO Prem rivals, the Etihad exec surprised those present by standing up to make a declaration.

In what was an implicit confirmation that the Prem’s independent commission has ruled that City were guilty of the vast majority of the 130 allegations of breaching financial rules, Soriano told the room that he felt he had to make a brief statement.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to sources who were present at the meeting, Soriano said he wanted to make it clear that he disagreed with the ruling of the commission, and that he and City were confident of eventually winning their battle.



The Spaniard then added: “It’s taken eight years to get there – and it’s going to take a lot more time.”

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho’s career ‘hits new low as ex-Man Utd and Chelsea star rejected by Russian team’ after training at FLIXTON
Sports.content:
Next

JADON SANCHO remains a free agent after reportedly being turned down by Russian side Krasnodar.

The winger, 26, was released by Manchester United in the summer after spending last season on loan at Aston Villa.



His United exit came nearly two years after his last appearance for the club, a late cameo in the 2024 Community Shield.

Despite being available on a free transfer, Sancho is yet to find a new club.



According to Spanish outlet AS, the former England international was offered to Krasnodar.

But the Russian Premier League leaders are said to have declined the opportunity.



In a bid to stay fit over the summer, Sancho trained at 10th tier Flixton FC’s facilities – a stone’s throw away from Carrington.

The non-League side subsequently praised his conduct, revealing in a statement: “After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

“Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of.

“He deserves respect both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Our doors will always be open to him.”

Sancho has been linked with several clubs this summer.

Last month it was claimed that he was nearing a switch to Brazilian side Palmeiras, only for the move not to materialise.

The 23-cap ex-Three Lion was also linked with former club Borussia Dortmund, but that transfer also failed to come together.



Sancho won a Bundesliga title and reached the Champions League final during his initial spell in Germany, and returned to BVB on loan in 2024.

He subsequently enjoyed further loan spells with Chelsea and Aston Villa, picking up Conference League and Europa League medals in the process.

Last season he made 23 Premier League appearances for Villa, failing to score and laying on two assists.

Sancho did play in all but two of Villa’s Europa League matches on their way to winning it, however, including a cameo in the final.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand hits back at Roy Keane and Thomas Tuchel over brutal Cole Palmer blasts amid England squad debate
Sports.content:
Next

RIO FERDINAND has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following public criticism from England boss Thomas Tuchel.

The Chelsea winger was one of the major omissions from Tuchel’s squad for last summer’s World Cup.



He was recalled to the fold for this round of international fixtures but withdrew with a minor injury, which prompted his gaffer to say: “He misses too many opportunities. I don’t blame him for it. It is just a fact.

“He misses way too many camps with injuries, and I only want to rely on what I witness and see within in my team, and for that, you have to be in camp.



“And if you’re not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it when you are actually on the pitch with me. So yes, it is a missed opportunity.”

Palmer, 24, was also pilloried by Roy Keane ahead of The Three Lions’ Nations League defeat to Spain last weekend, with the Irishman insisting the winger won’t take the team to the “next level.”

But Ferdinand disagrees with his former Manchester United team-mate saying on his YouTube channel: “I don’t think there’s a squad that should be picked for England that Cole Palmer shouldn’t be in.

“I’m sorry, I just think he gives you something different.

“He gives you that ability to slice through defensive units that have been set up.

“He has the ability to see that pass. He does things that none of the other players can do.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Cole Palmer is a precocious talent and I think you need him in and around the squad.

“He’s a kid who doesn’t get fazed on the biggest stage as well, he’s got that bit of arrogance about him which you need.

‘I get you need to be fit and have that harmonious vibe in the squad but this kid… you wait for someone like him.

“I’m not saying he has to start, but, boy, I find it hard not to put him in. I think he’s a wonderful footballer.



“Roy might have seen him having a bad day against Brentford, but what this kid can do with a football is rare.”

Palmer’s England team-mates will be back in action this evening, taking on the Czech Republic in their second Nations League Group C game in Prague.

Sports.title: Man City in huge trouble after guilty verdict but spare thought for innocent fans & signings who face uncertain future
Sports.content:
Next

WE now know that there was a giant elephant in the Manchester City dressing room.

A gigantic pile of the stuff all the way up to the ceiling.



Leaving behind a stench that may never dissipate and certainly not for long after the shovels have been put to use.

If the findings of the independent commission — who spent two years weighing up evidence from both the Premier League and City — are as damning as expected, the guilty will pay a heavy price.



Not just in terms of City’s status because wholesale breaches of financial regulations — if confirmed — will surely bring a punishment that adds up to relegation.

Pending compensation claims adding up to hundreds of millions will further damage even City’s UAE owners, who will be viewed by many as complicit, if not the orchestrators of the entire approach.



But so, too, will the innocent suffer.

The fans, most of whom took the club’s protestations of outrage over the allegations levelled against them at face value.

While there are still some who want to believe this is all a plot by the dastardly “Red Cartel”, most recognise a different scenario now.

Yet none of those supporters sent the emails, wrote the contracts, signed off the accounts.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And nor did the players — left stunned and shocked by the news that had international dressing rooms across Europe and beyond chuntering over the weekend.

You have to assume they, or their agents, would have asked about the progress of the Prem’s case.

But nobody could possibly have known it was proceeding, even at a seemingly glacial pace.

Equally, players were surely also given assurances from the highest echelons of the club that there was nothing to worry about.

No need for relegation clauses.



Would Marc Guehi, Antoine Semenyo, Elliot Anderson — to name just three — have joined City if they were given even the tiniest of hints they might be playing in the Championship by August 2027?

Whatever happens now, however long it takes, everything about City has changed.

Those titles, those managers, those players.

What were Man City charged with? MAN CITY have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they were initially hit with. Those charges were upped to 130 and fit into the following six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

All compromised, undercut and permanently questioned.



Half a century ago, Brian Clough turned his first meeting with his new Leeds players into a warzone.

Old Big ’Ead stared Norman Hunter, Johnny Giles, Billy Bremner and Co in the face.

And Clough said: “You lot may all be internationals and have won all the domestic honours there are to win under Don Revie.

“But, as far as I’m concerned, the first thing you can do for me is chuck all your medals and all your caps and all your pots and all your pans into the biggest f***ing dustbin you can find.

“Because you’ve never won any of them fairly. You’ve done it all by cheating.”



Enzo Maresca has joined the Etihad giants three times since the Prem probe began.

And he will clearly not say anything of the sort to his squad when they return — presumably still in a state of shock — following this international break.

He does not have to.

Every rival fanbase, starting at Anfield on Sunday week, will do it for him.

A ceaseless, unrelenting barrage of abuse, placards, jeers and chants.



Sympathy, too, will be in short supply.

City may have won trophies with a swagger and delivered some remarkable, unforgettable teams and moments.

Yet long-standing suspicions over the mechanisms that led to that dominance have now, seemingly, been justified.

It also becomes clear just why City were so, so desperate to bring down Richard Masters and the Prem executive team, going out of their way to block and hinder the investigation.

The Wizard of Oz was all powerful until someone finally peeked behind the curtain.



Masters and Co wanted to pull it back with a mighty yank — exposing the whole shebang to the disinfectant of sunlight.

All we have seen, so far, is the shadows behind the scenes.

Not the evidence, the findings, the scale of the reported deceit that the probe appears to have found over many years.

For the good of football, the rest of it must be put in the full public spotlight quickly.

Everybody has waited far too long.



When it started, that elephant was a calf. Now it’s a fully-grown adult.

UTD LOOK RAT-TLED

SIR JIM RATCLIFFE has never been scared of hacking people off.

Even if it means his own sporting hero, Manchester United icon Eric Cantona, thinks he is a villain.

Like the proverbial scorpion, stinging the frog carrying him across the river, it’s in his nature.

The kid from Failsworth who turned himself into Britain’s richest man at one point, the head of a global conglomerate.



Billionaire Sir Jim, 73, has always adopted a ‘take no prisoners’ stance when it comes to business.

So it shouldn’t have been a shock that Ratcliffe and Ineos brought that attitude to their stewardship of United after buying a stake in February 2024.

Now, the reality is beginning to strike.



Fans have been on the verge of mutiny since the Glazers’ takeover in 2005.

If the white knight proves no better than the American dragons, their fury will be incandescent.

LEVY WITH LAST LAUGH

AN hour into the Premier League shareholders meeting — and a familiar face walked through the doors of the same central London hotel last week.

Whether Daniel Levy, former executive chairman of Tottenham, initially realised he was 20 yards from the room where it happens was unclear.

Although he gave a slightly nervous smile towards the small gaggle of journalists in the lobby.



But as one of the men who pushed Prem chiefs hardest to investigate Manchester City – and who lodged Spurs’ claim to push for compensation and damages if the chance arose – that smile might have been wider 24 hours later.

BEER WE GO

ANDY BURNHAM’S plan to lift the booze ban for people watching football matches brought plenty of reaction from both sides of the argument.

My Sun colleague Pete Nuttall argued he really didn’t want to be showered with beer from joyful Seagulls fans every time his Brighton side score.



Fair enough.

But every Spurs fan will tell you the Prime Minister’s proposal is not an issue if you’re going to stay bone dry all season.

FINAL THOUGHTS

AT LEAST one part of the World Cup “what if” has now been settled.

Fans had pondered how events might have played out in July’s Metlife final had England not lost to Argentina.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The answer now seems clear: a football match, not a Fight Club.



Fun to watch. And Spain winning… comfortably.

Sports.title: ‘Danger to ourselves’ – Thomas Tuchel warns leaky England defence after 13 goals conceded as two stars face injury race
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND manager Thomas Tuchel warned the Three Lions’ leaky defence they are a “danger” to themselves.

Tuchel’s men face the Czech ­Republic in the Nations League on Tuesday after Saturday’s 3-2 defeat to Spain made it 13 GOALS conceded in six games.



Manchester City pair Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly saw errors ­punished by Lamine Yamal and Dani Olmo at Wembley.

Boss Tuchel, 53, said: “We need to improve because when we had the ball we were the biggest danger to ­ourselves around the box.



“We just had too many individual mistakes when we had the ball, especially in the deep build-up.

“That is something we cannot repeat at this level. We have to be technically absolutely clinical under pressure.”



Guehi will keep his place in Prague despite being caught dithering as Yamal struck in the second minute.

Tuchel was keen to stick with the same back-four but Ezri Konsa and O’Reilly are fitness doubts.

He said: “They missed training with minor issues, which are still issues. They need to be assessed and we will take a decision.”

England have kept just four clean sheets in 13 games. But Tuchel saw some positives at the back despite conceding three goals to the world champions.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

He said: “In defending, I have no concerns and trust we can do it. Some players are not here that would help in organising the defensive block.

“Our defending was more disciplined, cohesive and organised than in some World Cup matches.

“We never lost our structure. The result was heavily influenced by some individual mistakes but that can happen.”

Jude Bellingham’s performance against Spain was a huge plus. He set up Anthony Gordon’s equaliser to add to three goals and three assists for Real Madrid this season.



Tuchel said: “He looks like a real member of the squad on and off the pitch. I liked his performance a lot.

“It was a bit of a new position for him where he can overload both sides. That suits him very well.”

After losing to Spain, England need a positive result against the Czechs to keep their Nations League hopes alive.

But Tuchel added: “It’s a bit early in the group for a ‘must win’.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Rio Ferdinand calls for a PETITION to get Tony Pulis trophy and demands Lescott ‘bring my b****y medal’
Sports.content:

MANCHESTER UNITED legend Rio Ferdinand insists rivals Man City should hand over their trophies and medals after being found guilty of breaching financial rules.

City were declared guilty on all but one of the 115 charges they have been facing since 2023 following a four-year investigation by an independent commission.



However, sanctions have yet to be finalised as Man City continue to maintain their innocence and plan to appeal.

Breaches of Uefa’s Financial Fair Play regulations and the Prem’s own Profitability and Sustainability Rules were also among the charges.



City are facing severe consequences, such as points deductions, fines and even EXPULSION from the English top flight.

The Citizens also face the prospect of having to hand over trophies won between 2009 and 2018, which is the period they were investigated for.

During those years, the Manchester giants won three Premier League titles, three League Cups, the FA Cup and the Community Shield.

The 2011 FA Cup was actually City’s first major honour since Emirati supremo Sheikh Mansour took over in 2008.

Man City beat Stoke 1-0 at Wembley thanks to Yaya Toure’s winner, but now many insist they should hand over the cup to the finalists.

Ferdinand, 47, is adamant Premier League cult hero Tony Pulis, who was in charge of the Potters that time, should be given the trophy.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

So much so that the star pundit is willing to start a petition so that Pulis, 68, can have his flowers.

Ferdinand tweeted: “Let’s start petition to get Tony Pulis is [sic] FA Cup Winners Medal!”

The England icon also argues the verdict means he is also due a seventh Premier League winners’ medal.

If City are stripped of their titles then Man Utd will add two more Premier League trophies to their cabinet as runners-up of the 2011/12 campaign and the 2017/18 season, while Liverpool will be due the 2013/14 honour.



Ferdinand was part of United’s 2012 team that finished second after Sergio Aguero’s famous winner against Queens Park Rangers sealed Man City’s first ever Prem gong.

But the legendary defender is adamant that title should be handed over and specifically targeted ex-England team-mate Joleon Lescott as he argued he should personally hand over his medal to the Man Utd great.

Ferdinand said on his Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast: “Next time Joleon’s on, he better bring my b***** medal.

“If you’re found guilty, then I think you should have to give the medals back.

“When I see Joleon, I’m actually going to go to his house and just say, ‘Listen, hand it over. Hand it over’.



“You can’t really sit there and say that you were champions, can you? Or you won this or you won that.

‘Well, they’re not going to have to pay any fines. They’re not going to get relegated.

“Just hand over the trophy. Hand over the medals, hand over the trophy. Simple as.”

Sports.title: Keenum rolls back years to lead Chicago Bears to win over Philadelphia Eagles
Sports.content:
Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first NFL start in almost three years as Chicago Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.

Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum starred completing 24 passes from 34 attempts to make 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a one-yard plunge with seven minutes and 19 seconds left to play, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.

It was Keenum's first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland in December 2023.

Sports.title: Divide and Conquer and Al Qayed clash at Bath
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Tuesday with action from Bath, Sedgefield and Wolverhampton, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.32 Bath - Talented pair Divide and Conquer and Al Qayed feature

Talented two-year-olds Divide And Conquer and Al Qayed feature in the British EBF Future Stayers' Novice Stakes.

This has proved an informative novice with Hopewell Rock winning in 2024 before subsequent Juddmonte International winner, Item taking the 2025 edition.

Of the raced runners, these two certainly bring the strongest form to the race. Al Qayed finished well behind the unbeaten Bin Jahwar on debut before improving to place third behind subsequent Royal Lodge third, Quicken Away.

He did not look totally comfortable on the heavy ground that day, as well as looking very raw so should take another step forward for the experience.

Victorious Forever filly, Divide And Conquer was bought for 320,000gns as a yearling. She showed a lot of talent on debut to finish second having been bumped a couple of times in the final half furlong. The third in that race has since won at Haydock and this filly can take a step forward on her second start.

Newcomers Political Resident and Next Best both contain a lot of stamina in their pedigrees and may need their first outings.

3.15 Sedgefield - Passengerontheship and Thank You Blue headline trappy affair

Passengerontheship and Thank You Blue headline a trappy Winning Connection Conference Hire Handicap Chase.

Passengerontheship progressed rapidly over fences midway through the year when landing a five-week fiver-timer, ending in late June. He has risen 28lb during this period before finding a mark of 110 too tough to overcome.

He stayed on well when last see, having been off the bridle from a fair way out and although he should remain competitive, that run suggests the drop back in trip is unlikely to suit.

In contrast, Thank You Blue could relish coming back in trip after finding a six-furlong step up too far. He had been shaping well before this, with a mistake at the last costing him on his penultimate start, and this nine-year-old could put up a career best effort over fences, with conditions to suit.

Tanking Along could prove a big player if coming on for his Cartmel effort last time. He is two from two at the track over fences and remains well-handicapped if returning to form.

Four Decades has shown very little over both hurdles and fences and very much requires a complete transformation to land this contest.

5.30 Wolverhampton - Saeed bin Suroor's well-bred Arabian Summer returns off 23-month lay-off

Saeed bin Suroor's well-bred Arabian Summer returns off a 23-month lay-off in the attheraces.com/marketmovers Maiden Stakes.

Arabian Summer is a half-sister to Prix Chaudenay winner and Dubai Gold Cup second, Manobo, but showed some speed at six furlongs on debut, and Saeed bin Suroor is very skilful in preparing his horses after a lengthy lay-off. She could be a player, although it should be tricky against race fit rivals.

Despite being the most exposed, Gold Star Glazing sets a half-decent standard, bumping into the promising Wathnan owned Storm Force last time out. He can put his experience to good use and improve back at seven furlongs.

Battlefield Boy perhaps made the most promising debut when third at Lingfield earlier this month, and Missmisfortune also shaped similarly when third on debut at Kempton.

Best of the rest

2.02 Bath - Decalogue aims to continue his progression following Kempton success.

4.02 Bath - In-form trio Maharajas Express, South Shore and Alondra contest competitive sprint Handicap.

4.15 Sedgefield - Jet Of Dreams attempts to repeat last year's success back down to the same mark.

4.45 Sedgefield - Close House and Red Shea bid to build on promising bumper debuts.

Chantilly - Informative maidens and Listed contest.

Marseille-Borely - Seven-race card.

Sports.title: Antonelli vows to ‘re-establish the order’ over Russell at Bahrain GP
Sports.content:
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan.

Antonelli had finished ahead of Russell in five successive Grands Prix but could only manage fifth in Baku, as the Brit produced his best weekend of the season to claim victory from pole position. The result cut Antonelli's lead over his Mercedes team-mate to 66 points with eight rounds remaining.

Although he salvaged some points, Antonelli's performance left plenty of room for improvement ahead of the second leg of the triple-header, with Malaysia set to host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Asked whether Russell is now his only title rival after Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton dropped more than 100 points back, Antonelli said: "He's always been my rival.

"But I'll make sure next week I re-establish the order and just make sure that I will be at back at my usual level because this weekend I was driving more like my grandma, so it wasn't the usual Kimi.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Luckily we have another race coming up, and I'm really looking forward to it."

The 20-year-old Italian endured a scrappy weekend, missing a major chunk of track time in practice because of a technical issue before crashing in the first part of qualifying to leave himself starting from 16th on the grid.

"FP1 I did three laps and then missed the half of FP2," Antonelli added. "In FP3, I was getting to the rhythm.

"And then in qualifying, that Q1 one lap was actually okay. But I did a mistake, and then again you re-enter in the bad loop.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP.

"Then in the race, I didn't have the confidence, and I just at drove 80 per cent the whole time.

"Realistically, I wasn't there mentally to be able to push 100 per cent as well because I just didn't have the confidence that I had previous weekends, but it will be much better in Sepang."

'Exciting to see battle resume in Malaysia'

Russell underlined his pre-season status as the clear title favourite by winning the season opener in Australia, only to be stunned as Antonelli then claimed the first five victories of his career in successive races.

The Italian remains in control of the title race and has also appeared to hold a race-pace advantage over Russell at almost every circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell just beat Max Verstappen to victory by one tenth of a second.

That finally changed in Baku, where Russell backed up a solid run of form by being faster than Antonelli at every stage of the weekend.

Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord insists the strength of Russell's performance won't amount to a psychological blow for Antonelli.

"I don't really think it makes a difference," said Lord, who address the media in Baku in the absence of team boss Toto Wolff.

"I think the drivers, they're setting themselves their own high standards, and they want to perform to those.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater gives his verdict after the Azerbaijan GP, where George Russell pipped Max Verstappen to victory.

"One of the great assets and the great strengths of this team is we've got two drivers who are capable of fighting at the very front, putting the car on pole, delivering flawless race wins, and that's part of the strength of the team.

"Kimi put it behind him and did a great job in the race. George did an incredible job out front, and it'll be exciting to see them going at it in Malaysia."

Sports.title: Whyte wants Fisher after injury hell - 'I fought Itauma with a broken foot!'
Sports.content:
Dillian Whyte provided a gruesome description while explaining the agonising injury that he suffered, just weeks before his last fight against Moses Itauma.

"It felt like someone had dropped a dumbbell on my foot," revealed Whyte when asked to put into words the pain caused by the fractured foot that he sustained in training last summer.

"I was running and I felt it [my foot] and then I went to spar and I was sparring big, agile guys and someone was pressing me, I stepped back the wrong way and then it just fractured clean.

"It was terrible, but we're used to pulling off miracles. We're used to fighting injured.

"I made the best of the situation and had a decent camp. I felt good during fight week and really thought I would beat Moses."

Whyte has entered the ring before with debilitating injuries. He famously fought bitter rival Anthony Joshua whilst being hampered by a badly damaged shoulder and other grim wounds have been overcome in a heavyweight career that led him to become two-time WBC interim world champion.

But the Brixton man could not shrug off the effects of his injured foot and the bone fractured again while he was limbering up in the dressing room, only hours before he was due to face Itauma in Saudi Arabia last August.

"I started warming up, jumped a little bit of rope, and then reinjured the foot. Completely fractured it again," said Whyte.

"We had to call the doctor who was with me to examine it. He advised me not to fight and I said 'no'. There's no way I'm going to come all the way to Saudi and not fight last minute.

"I was confident that I would still be able to drag Moses into the later rounds and stop him as [Filip] Hrgovic recently did."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dillian Whyte has welcomed a heavyweight showdown with Johnny Fisher and believes it will be 'exciting while it lasts'

Whyte tried to conceal his damaged foot, which had been heavily strapped, but his lack of mobility was exposed by Itauma, who piled on a succession of punches before the bout was waved off in the opening round.

While Itauma celebrated his victory, Whyte remained silent about his significant injury and has been absent from the ring since that fight.

"I didn't want to mention it, go into it, and take away from his win, because he done alright. I got clocked and he won the fight.

"I didn't want to go on too much about it and I think people got carried away with the fact that I got beat in a round by Moses.

"I don't think people would draw the same conclusions if they had the full facts.

"People have short memories and they like to say 'retire because of this, retire because of that' but what they don't realise is we're members of a rare generation of entertaining British heavyweight boxers that are coming to the end of our careers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dillian Whyte believes that rumours the fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could fall through is nothing more than mind games - and gives his prediction for the fight

"I love boxing and I'll fight anyone. Be grateful that you have guys like me around because when we're gone, there will be a long drought in the heavyweight division."

Johnny Fisher called for the return of Whyte last week, insisting that there is a 'good chance' the fight could happen in the near future.

Whyte readily accepted the verbal challenge and was watching from ringside as Fisher battled to a majority decision victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena last weekend.

"Credit to Johnny Fisher, because he's a big lump, he hasn't had time to learn a lot, but he's got a lot of courage, he's got a lot of heart, he's a big puncher and he's brave," said Whyte, who is open to facing Fisher in November or December this year.

"He's a bit frantic and that, but he's very brave and he's a big guy who punches hard. When the fight gets tough, he keeps trying and he keeps coming back.

"You can never overlook that but let's be honest, I will knock Johnny Fisher out, simple as that."

Image: Dillian Whyte's manager Mike Ofo is hopeful that a fight against Johnny Fisher will be next

Whyte was joined by manager Michael Ofo, who says the fight has already been verbally accepted by Fisher's team and is hopeful it can be finalised.

"The fight was agreed in principle following Fisher's win on Saturday night with a handshake between me and Fisher's manager Adam Morallee," said Ofo.

"I was unsure whether Fisher and his management would take the fight, in spite of Fisher having called Dillian out, so I called Adam over and asked him. He immediately responded: 'Absolutely. Let's do it next!'

"It would be a huge all-British clash and a massive event for London. So, let's stop talking and get it on!"

Sports.title: Littler in shock first-round exit at World Grand Prix as Van Gerwen also beaten
Sports.content:
Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated.

Littler won the first set, but was far from his best as Woodhouse spurned several chances at double to have taken the opener into a deciding leg.

Woodhouse made no mistake in sets two and three, however, to see him pull off one of the biggest upsets in the hostory of the double-in, double-out tournament.

Image: Littler's World Grand Prix defence was ended at the first hurdle by Woodhouse

He'll face former finalist Nathan Aspinall in the second round after he overcame Kevin Doets in a final-leg decider earlier on the opening night.

Following his stunning early exit, Littler posted on his Instagram: "Well played @lukewoodly180 was a good game, good one to be apart of aswell.

"Both hit, both missed but Luke took his chance and nice week off now, all the best to Luke for rest of tournament."

Littler followed that up by signalling his intent to now attend the Super League Grand Final on Saturday, which features his beloved Warrington Wolves - and would have clashed with the Grand Prix semi-finals.

"May aswell get myself to OT [Old Trafford] now I'm out. Let's go the Wire @warringtonrlfc," Littler added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking back in February, Littler looked ahead to the Super League season and correctly predicted Warrington Wolves would make it to Old Trafford

Following his seismic victory over Littler, Woodhouse said afterwards: "Luke's not a robot. He's going to have days and weeks and whatever where he's not right on it.

"But people have echoed it and I'm going to say it again, he's one of a kind, Luke.

"I hope people will take the time to appreciate how good he is and not give him a hard time. You might not see another Luke Littler ever again."

Van Gerwen dumped out but Price, Clayton win

Elsewhere, not only were Van Gerwen's hopes of a seventh Grand Prix crown dashed but he suffered a third-straight first-round loss in the tournament as Ryan Joyce came back from a set down to defeat the Dutchman.

Welsh duo Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton, winners of the Grand Prix in 2020 and 2021 respectively, also progressed, with Price putting in the performance of the night as he averaged 101.61 and dropped only one leg in beating Sebastian Bialecki.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price hit two huge 120 checkouts in his dominant opening-night victory

Clayton was made to work much harder by Krzysztof Ratajski, one of six matches (out of eight) to go the distance on the opening night.

Cameron Menzies and Kevin Doets both missed match darts when losing out to Ross Smith and Aspinall, respectively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies nails 158 to take an early lead against Ross Smith

Each had chances to wrap up two-set victories, but Menzies missed two looks at tops before Smith swept him aside 3-0 in the deciding set, while Doets spurned three match darts - including a wild miss at bullseye - and Aspinall would ultimately take it in a last-leg decider in the third set.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nathan Aspinall wins a messy set to stay alive against Kevin Doets

Danny Noppert came flying out of the blocks to open the night, claiming five consecutive legs before Niko Springer, out of nowhere, claimed the next three to take the second set, before normal service resumed in the third.

Wessel Nijman, meanwhile, rounded off the evening with a routine 2-0 victory over Rob Cross.

He'll face Clayton next, while Noppert takes on MVG conqueror Joyce and Price goes up against Smith, who revealed he almost pulled out of the World Grand Prix after being hospitalised in the week leading up to the tournament.

"I've had a week from hell," Smith said after his first-round victory. "I've come home and picked up some sort of virus and I've had a few issues with my heart as well.

"I was in hospital on Friday. I thought I was pulling out of this event on Saturday, so to be here is an achievement in itself. Let alone play and win like that, I'm very happy."
