Sports.title: Mallorca goalkeeper taken to hospital with serious head injury after canteen structure collapses
Sports.content:
Mallorca goalkeeper taken to hospital with serious head injury after canteen structure collapses

Mallorca goalkeeper Ivan Cuellar has been hospitalised after a bizarre incident at the club's training ground.

A section of decor within the facility's canteen collapsed, leaving Cuellar with a head injury.



3 Mallorca goalkeeper Cuellar has been hospitalised after a piece of canteen decor collapsed Credit: Getty

The club confirmed that the incident occurred at Mallorca's Son Bibiloni base.

Cuellar will now remain under observation for 24 hours after being taken to hospital for treatment.

The decoration inside the canteen was described as a 'large structure' by the Spanish second-tier side.



Mallorca statement

A statement released by Mallorca read: "This morning, Ivan ‘Pichu’ Cuellar suffered a serious head injury after a large ​structure, which formed part of the decor in the dining room at the Ciutat Esportiva collapsed.

"The ⁠player has been taken to hospital for treatment ​and ​will remain under observation ​for the next 24 hours."



The injury to Cuellar comes as Mallorca prepare to face Girona on the road this weekend.

They travel to Catalonia on Sunday, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm.

If Cuellar is deemed unfit to play due to the head injury, Mallorca will be left with just one available senior goalkeeper.



Arnau Tenas is currently the only option between the posts for manager Luis Garcia.

In addition to Cuellar's injury, fellow stopper Lucas Bergstrom, formerly of Chelsea, is currently on international duty with Finland.

3 Cuellar will remain under observation after the incident at the club's training ground Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, the incident follows a 1-0 home defeat to Almeria on Sunday.



The result leaves them sixth in the Segunda Division after seven matches this season.

Mallorca are competing outside LaLiga for the first time since 2021 following relegation last term.

Who is Ivan Cuellar?

Cuellar is into his fourth season with Mallorca having joined the club from Sporting Gijon back in 2023.

He has also previously had spells with Eibar and Leganes and started his senior career with Atletico Madrid.



Since signing for Mallorca, the 42-year-old has made just three competitive appearances for the club.

3 Cuellar joined Mallorca in 2023 and has made three first-team appearances for the club Credit: Getty

Cuellar has also been an unused substitute in each of their opening seven matches of the current campaign.

The veteran stopper previously won three caps for Spain at Under-21 level at the beginning of his career.



His current Mallorca deal expires at the end of the season after he signed a one-year extension in July.

Sports.title: Hungary player writhing in pain stretchered off after ten minutes of treatment
Sports.content:
Hungary player writhing in pain stretchered off after ten minutes of treatment

It was a night to forget for Bendeguz Bolla in Hungary's Nations League game against Northern Ireland as he was made to wait for stretcher.

Isaac Price went to tackle the right-back and slid in to make the challenge, but he caught Bolla's foot, dragging his ankle underneath him.



3 The medical staff eventually managed to get Bolla the treatment he required Credit: Getty

The incident happened in the 31st minute of the 0-0 draw, and Bolla received some treatment on the pitch before attempting to carry on.

He didn't last long as in the 34th minute, Attila Osvath replaced him.

The Rapid Wien full-back limped off and waited behind the goal until the medical staff managed to get a stretcher over there and take him away.



But by the time he was led away from the pitch to receive more appropriate medical care, it had been six further minutes since he was taken off.

It has was a fiery old game at Windsor Park in Belfast with a challenge on Daniel Lukacs sparking a scuffle right at the end of the first half.



The referee blew his whistle for the end of the first 45 minutes, but that didn't stop Shea Charles from barrelling into an aerial challenge.

The Hungary striker never saw his man coming, and he ended up in a heap, which the visitors didn't like at all.



It sparked a mini brawl with Lukacs sprawled on the floor, with the forward taking a long time to get up after his teammates had already disappeared for half time.

3 Lukacs did come out for the second half to carry on

3 Charles summed up the aggressive nature of Northern Ireland

Big opportunity

Northern Ireland started their Nations League campaign off in perfect fashion with a shock 1-0 win away against Georgia.



Michael O'Neill's side scored in the last minute of stoppage time through Charles.

It meant a win over Hungary would have taken them clear at the top of the group with Ukraine and Georgia playing out a goalless draw earlier on Monday.

They are now level on points with Ukraine at the top of the table and they play them on Friday in a game that could decide their fate for the rest of the campaign as they head to Slovakia to face them.

Nations League rewards

Northern Ireland are in division B of the Nations League, which means should they top their group, they'll be promoted to division A and play all of Europe's best teams.



But there is a further incentive which is very important for teams like Northern Ireland.

For this edition of the Nations League, the group winners of the lower tiers all get a safety net when it comes to qualifying for the European Championship.

So if they mess up their qualifying campaign, they will have a spot in the qualification play-offs.

That adds something extra to these Nations League games and why a win for O'Neill's men would have been so big.

Sports.title: Italian giants set for £1billion super stadium to host Euro 2032
Sports.content:
Roma are set to leave the Stadio Olimpico for a new £1billion super stadium, which will host the 2032 European Championship.

The Italian giants have played at the city's Olympic stadium since 1953, but they will finally leave for pastures new after a mega ground was approved.

1 Rome's Stadio Olimpico hosts Roma and Lazio for their home Serie A games Credit: Getty

However, it has never been truly theirs, with the club having to share it with bitter rivals Lazio, the national team as well as the men's rugby side as well.

But this new stadium is set to have a 60,000 capacity and it has received final approval.

It will be a huge project costing £1.17billion with construction planned to start in March 2027.

The plan is for the construction to take two and a half years and be open in 2029 for Roma to move in and claim their own home, possibly in time for the start of the 2029/30 season.

Rome's Mayor Roberto Gualtieri confirmed the decision after a conference on Monday.

He said: “This is the first large, new facility that will elevate Rome’s footballing scene and represent a significant redevelopment of a part of our city.

“The conditions are now in place to proceed expeditiously and begin construction in early 2027, and have the stadium ready in three years. Construction will last precisely two and a half years, so the stadium could be ready as early as 2029.”

And those sentiments were echoed by Italy's Minister for Sport and Youth, Andrea Abodi, who said: “Yes, it was a great team effort, as was done for the Jubilee; all the institutions collaborated.

"This was about finally completing a long-awaited project: our thoughts turn to Dino Viola and Franco Sensi. This is a great result for all Roma fans, obviously, but also for the entire city and the country.

"It marks a process of modernisation for the city and also of extremely important social and environmental redevelopment. A very large, very beautiful park will be created, available to all citizens.

"Truly, it is a very important result: we will continue with determination until the end, until the inauguration of the stadium.”

He then added: “All the conditions are in place because now we will start the tender, and in parallel there will be the verification of the TFTE, the executive report, and after these steps the construction work will begin.

"All the conditions are in place to stick to the schedule; it’s a two-and-a-half-year program: in three years, the stadium can be ready. Three years from now, by the calculations, we are at the end of 2029.

"The construction site lasts two and a half years, if we start in spring 2027, do the math: it could even be ready at the end of 2029."

Roma's bright future

The Stadio Olimpico has provided some magical moments for Roma.

Francesco Totti played all of his home games there, and they celebrated their first European trophy at the ground as well.

But with Italy co-hosting the 2032 edition of the European Championship, the government want new, modern stadiums.

As such, Roma, also owned by Everton owner Dan Friedkin, aren't the only huge Italian club getting a new ground, with the San Siro being demolished.

That iconic venue currently hosts AC Milan and Inter Milan, and the construction of the new ground on the same site is set to begin next year.

Again, the plan is for that to be ready in time for the Euro 2032 with Italy co-hosting the tournament alongside Turkey.

Sports.title: Where every Man City player should go if they’re forced to sell top stars including Erling Haaland
Sports.content:
Where every Man City player should go if they’re forced to sell top stars including Erling Haaland

Manchester City would be forced into a transfer fire sale if the worst were to happen to them and the club are relegated.

But talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor has offered a helping hand to solve one of their issues - by detailing each of their stars' next moves.



9 City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak will be taking a plethora of calls from agents and players

On Friday, it was revealed that City were found guilty of the overwhelming majority of the 115 charges they faced relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

Enzo Maresca's side were initially charged in February 2023 with alleged breaches between a period of 2009 to 2018.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak continues to maintain the club's innocence, however, the Premier League have been pushing for a record-points deduction, which could see the club relegated.



talkSPORT revealed on Sunday that Erling Haaland and Co. do not have relegation release clauses in their contracts - which means a wave of transfers would need to be negotiated with rival teams.

Breakfast host Agbonlahor said: "If they get the punishments that we think they will get and they do get relegated, and they go down to League Two, these players are going to leave - a lot of these players. If we're being realistic, this could happen."



Gianluigi Donnarumma - Man United

The Red Devils have only just snared Karim Cassim away from the Etihad Stadium - but it's extremely rare for a senior player to cross the divide.

Yet question marks over Senne Lammens has Agbonlahor believing Donnarumma could do a reverse of Peter Schmeichel.



The Italian, a former Man United target, has kept 17 clean sheets in 39 appearances since joining City from Paris Saint-Germain in 2025.

"I've been watching Lammens - poor at the World Cup; cost Belgium in that game [against Spain], and he's not being great this season.

"Look at Lisandro Martinez own goal against Fulham. He's got to do better with that save. I'm not convinced in him.

"I will say Donnarumma to Manchester United. If I'm Manchester United, go and nick their number one goalkeeper!"



9 Donnarumma helped City to a famous 1-0 win at Old Trafford earlier this month Credit: AFP

Ruben Dias - Al Nassr

The 29-year-old is now one of the longest-serving players at the club and one of only four stars remaining from the 2023 treble winners.

He committed his future to City in 2025 with a contract extension until 2029, but he hasn't been backed to stay if they are relegated.

Agbonlahor remarked: "He's not the same Ruben Dias from three, four years ago. He's getting on a bit now.



"I would say Saudi Arabia - go and sign with Cristiano Ronaldo, your Portuguese teammate. Go and settle off into the sun."

Pressed by Ally McCoist on whether Dias was better than that level, Agbonlahor replied: "Yeah, but I think it makes sense with his age."

9 Dias could join countrymen Ronaldo, Joao Felix and Samu Costa at Al Nassr Credit: Getty

Marc Guehi - Aston Villa

talkSPORT's Tony Cascarino believes Guehi has not been the same player since joining City from Crystal Palace in January.



An opportunity to rediscover his Eagles form could present itself at Agbonlahor's old club, Aston Villa, as a replacement for his England defensive partner, Ezri Konsa, at club level.

"Champions League football; we'll have you over," Agbonlahor said.

"You can compete with Pau Torres, [Tyrone] Mings, [Taylor] Harwood-Bellis, and [Victor] Lindelof."

9 Guehi has scored one goal in five Premier League appearances this season Credit: Getty

Nico O'Reilly - Liverpool

This one would really sting for City fans if one of their own jumps ship after becoming such a force for both club and country.



Having come through the Etihad academy set-up as a midfielder, O'Reilly flourished as an unorthodox left-back with five goals and three assists in 31 Premier League appearances.

He also scored a game-deciding double in City's Carabao Cup final win in March, and was a key part of England's World Cup campaign - despite only making his first senior international start last November.

Agbonlahor told talkSPORT: "O'Reilly - Liverpool. They're dying for a left-back, [Kostas] Tsimikas is their second choice.

"[Milos] Kerkez hasn't been at the level. I think that'd be a great move."



9 O'Reilly has enjoyed a meteoric rise since coming through the City ranks Credit: Getty

Rest of the defenders

Rayan Aït-Nouri, who has been sent home early from international duty with Algeria, and was also the subject of an audacious enquiry to City from United in the summer, was tipped to join Tottenham.

Destiny Udogie has struggled with fitness issues in recent years, having only started just one Premier League game this season.

Andy Robertson, meanwhile, hasn't yet rediscovered his Liverpool form since arriving on a free transfer this summer.



'I can see Khusanov in a Bayern shirt'

Elsewhere, Josko Gvardiol was backed for Barcelona, who 'always need cover in defence', according to talkSPORT's Agbonlahor.

Agbonlahor continued: "I look at [Abdukodir] Khusanov, I say Bayern Munich. I see him as a Vincent Kompany sort of player.

"Aggressive like Vincent Kompany, he's got the speed as well. I can see him in a Bayern Munich shirt. Rico Lewis, I think you stay.

"City through and through. You stay at Man City, and you bring them back to the Premier League from League Two - proper legend!"



9 Lewis was backed to emulate Lee Wallace, who stayed at Rangers in 2012 despite the club's demotion to the Scottish Third Division Credit: Getty

Elliot Anderson - Man United

The England international attracted strong interest from the Red Devils prior to his £116m switch to their local rivals last summer.

Agbonlahor added: “Elliot Anderson – Manchester United wanted you, now you go there.

“Manchester United – you wanted Elliot Anderson, go and get him for maybe half the price.”



9 Anderson had been on United's wish list but opted to join Manchester City in a £116m deal Credit: Getty

Rayan Cherki - Real Madrid

France manager Zinedine Zidane has hailed Cherki as a 'real baller' whom he would have loved to have played with as a player.

And Agbonlahor believes the 1998 Ballon d'Or winner could prove to be the difference-maker in swaying his compatriot to his old club.

"Zidane would definitely advise him to go to Real Madrid. I can picture him." Where's he playing? Is he walking into that team?



"He's not walking into it but competition," Agbonlahor replied when asked by McCoist where Cherki would play at the Bernabeu.

"He can come up one of the wings and play with [Jude] Bellingham and [Kylian] Mbappe."

Enzo Fernandez - Bayern Munich

"I can picture him there, Ally," Agbonlahor continued. "[Mateo] Kovacic into his 30s I say Saudi Arabia."

"Matheus Nunes, I say Aston Villa - versatile, can play at right-back and would be competition for [Aaron] Wan-Bissaka and [Matty] Cash.



"Can also play centre-midfield; I think he prefers playing there. [Ayyoub] Bouaddi - PSG."

9 Fernandez and Cherki have been backed to join Bayern and Madrid, respectively Credit: Getty

Erling Haaland - Real Madrid or Barcelona

talkSPORT previously reported that Barcelona were keen on signing Haaland, who has eight years left on his contract at the Etihad.

Barca are still looking to replace Robert Lewandowski following his move to Major League Soccer side Chicago Fire last summer.



But Agbonlahor initially said it was a 'no-brainer' that Haaland would end up at their LaLiga rivals Madrid alongside Cherki.

"I could picture him there, the main man - Mbappe off him? Cherki, Bellingham... Barca as well, great shout.

"They haven't really replaced Lewandowski, have they? Even though they've signed Gabriel Jesus, but he's not at the level."

9 Haaland has continued his goalscoring form into the new season, scoring five goals in his first five Premier League outings Credit: Getty



Ndiaye to Chelsea and Doku to Arsenal

Phil Foden was urged to follow fellow academy graduate Lewis in staying to get Man City back to the Premier League.

But his fellow wide attackers may all be pinched by English rivals in Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool all looking to boost their front lines.

Agbonlahor told talkSPORT: "[Iliman] Ndiaye, I'm saying Chelsea. Chelsea could do with other options, couldn't they?

"[Morgan] Rogers, [Cole] Palmer very good, and Joao Pedro - could do with another attacker in there as well.



"Then Jeremy Doku [to] Arsenal. Arsenal need a left winger. They need someone, a different option to [Christos] Tzolis.

"So I think that'll be a perfect signing for Arsenal. Just go in there.

"Then I'm going [Antoine] Semenyo to Liverpool. He walks into their side - left-hand side or right and he's the perfect player for Liverpool.

"So if they do get the charges and they do go into League Two, I think there's some great business there for some of the Premier League greats."

Sports.title: James Trafford's big chance: Leeds keeper set to start for England in Prague knowing that whatever happens, Jordan Pickford will return for the next two games. So can he now make his case to be No1 for good?
Sports.content:
James Trafford's big chance: Leeds keeper set to start for England in Prague knowing that whatever happens, Jordan Pickford will return for the next two games. So can he now make his case to be No1 for good?

When it comes to grabbing anything with both hands you would expect goalkeepers to be at an advantage, what with the big gloves and all that practice.

Opportunities to challenge Jordan Pickford as England's number one however tend to slip through.

Maybe modern keepers spend too much time learning to punch things clear or passing it about at the back to claim anything cleanly nowadays.

Dean Henderson has seemed close at times. Nick Pope and Aaron Ramsdale had their moments. Sam Johnstone's and Alex McCarthy's were more fleeting.

In Prague against Czechia, the chance belongs to James Trafford for the second time in four days and it can only be positive for England if he can deliver a performance to create at least some semblance of competition for the No1 shirt.

Pickford's dominance is stressed by this nugget of trivia doing the rounds after Saturday's 3-2 defeat by Spain: On each of the last five occasions England have conceded three or more, Pickford has been absent.

James Trafford will start in goal for England against Czechia with a chance to stake his claim

Henderson was in goal for two of them, Pope and Ramsdale for one each and now Trafford, although he did at least emerge with some credit from the Spain game.

There were smart early saves when Thomas Tuchel's team were in a mess and confidence to demand the ball at his feet, although England's young keeper must take his share of the collective blame for the fraught opening phase at Wembley.

Even if he was under instruction to play with risk and invite the Spanish press by delaying the release of his passes, the decisions he made under pressure did nothing at all to suggest his presence in goal would offer a more soothing experience than Pickford's trademark hyperactivity.

In Prague on Tuesday it will likely be a very different type of contest.

The Czechs have a new Spanish coach. Santi Denia spent 14 years in charge of various age levels of Spain youth teams including the U21s beaten by an England side including Trafford in the 2023 Euros final but are entering a new reset phase and are not expected to possess the slick cohesion and authority of the world champions.

Perhaps that was the appeal of this two-game strategy as Tuchel studies Trafford in two very different international environments. Once at home against the best around, the other away in a place where England will represent a prized scalp.

Tuchel has confirmed that unless something goes awry, Pickford will return against Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday and for the return against Czechia at Wembley, which will take his haul to 93 caps.

At 32, there is time on his side to cruise past Peter Shilton's 125-cap record if he can keep swatting aside the young challengers.

He is trying to break past Jordan Pickford (right) to become England's permanent No1

Pickford has proved a very capable England goalkeeper, matured into the role and is without doubt better for all the experience but his place has rarely been under serious threat.

Trafford must come with other ideas. He must dislodge his mate. His stars have belatedly aligned, playing regular Premier League football in a strong team with a commitment to defend properly.

This is more than half the battle because all jokes about missed opportunities aside they are truly scarce for homegrown goalkeepers in elite competition.

He rode out a difficult season in the Premier League with Burnley to excel as they bounced back from relegation by winning the Championship only to be set back again when Pep Guardiola lured him back to Manchester City then swerved to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma and relegate Trafford to his domestic cup keeper and cover.

'I won two trophies,' replied Trafford in a flash when reminded of this. 'It obviously wasn't ideal how it panned out but looking back I got two trophies to my name, so you take the positives and you play the cards you're dealt.'

Even so, this time last year he was playing for City in Carabao Cup ties at Huddersfield and Swansea, which was hardly ever going to convince Tuchel to wave him in past Pickford and Henderson of Crystal Palace, who is missing from this squad through injury.

At 23, Trafford is the same age Pickford was when he first broke in and made a debut against Germany in November 2017 four days before Joe Hart won his final cap, then won the spring auditions with Jack Butland and Pope to start in the 2018 World Cup.

Pickford seized his moment. Can Trafford do the same?

Sports.title: ECB chief Richard Thompson calls for a new charity event in the cricket calendar after walking 100 laps of Lord's to raise money for the Alzheimer's Society
Sports.content:
ECB chief Richard Thompson calls for a new charity event in the cricket calendar after walking 100 laps of Lord's to raise money for the Alzheimer's Society

ECB chairman Richard Thompson wants to establish a new high-profile charity event on the cricket calendar after walking 100 laps of Lord's – the equivalent of 31 miles – to raise money for the Alzheimer's Society.

Thompson, who lost both parents to dementia – including his mother as recently as three weeks ago – intends to challenge his counterparts at other national boards to do the walk themselves, and has visions of extending the event to venues such as Australia's MCG and Barbados's Kensington Oval.

'It occurred to me that a hundred at Lord's is the pinnacle for any batsman to achieve, so could we do 100 laps?' he told Daily Mail Sport, as he and 99 others walked anti-clockwise round cricket's most famous ground.

'It's clearly captured people's imagination, and we've already raised £300,000, which is £50,000 over where we thought we'd get.

'The purpose behind this is to make this an annual event at Lord's – and maybe to make it almost the ice-bucket-challenge principle. So I'm going to challenge the chair of Cricket Australia or the chair of Cricket West Indies: you come to Lord's, I come to Bridgetown, and we get 100 people to do it there, and then this becomes a more global annual event.'

ECB chairman Richard Thompson wants to establish a new high-profile charity event on the cricket calendar after walking 100 laps of Lord's to raise money for the Alzheimer's Society

Dementia is the UK's biggest killer, with Alzheimer's disease the most common form of dementia'.

'Trying to get a diagnosis is a nightmare,' said Thompson, who is also the founder and chair of Sport United Against Dementia. 'If you can be diagnosed early, there is a drug that slows down onset and so gives you a quality of life you might otherwise not have.

'But there are too many people in the country that don't want to know they've got it. I think there's still a stigma attached to it, where people sometimes don't want to admit that their parent or loved one is suffering from this, because their decline can be very noticeable.'

Sports.title: First Premier League owner breaks silence on Man City's 115 verdict: Hull City boss insists rivals 'no different to a doping athlete'
Sports.content:
First Premier League owner breaks silence on Man City's 115 verdict: Hull City boss insists rivals 'no different to a doping athlete'

Man City are no different to an Olympic athlete found guilty of doping, according to Hull City owner Acun Ilicali.

In referring to City's charges, of which the club have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115, Ilicali became the first Premier League owner to break his silence on the story engulfing football.

While City maintain their innocence and are expected to appeal, Ilicali categorised the charges as 'financial doping'.

He told the 1904 Club podcast: 'I don’t say they are guilty or not because they are saying they are innocent… and I think the Premier League says they are not innocent.

'If they are not innocent and they did something… I think [it is] not different than having doping and [winning] the Olympic medal.

'This is financial doping at the end of the day. Bringing top four or five players with huge money, breaking the rules. From that side, it doesn’t look very positive.'

Hull owner Acun Ilicali (left), pictured this season with wife Ayca Cagla Altunkaya, compared Man City's charges with an athlete doping

Ilicali has owned Hull since 2022 but the Tigers were relegated from the Premier League in 2014-15 and 2016-17 – two seasons in which City are accused of breaking the rules.

He said there are 'crazy advantages' for richer clubs, adding: 'As an owner, I shouldn’t speak too much about it, I think, because I’m not inside it to know everything about it in detail. From my side, I will make a general speech, which is if something involved in football is unfair… it should be punished.

'If you give a small punishment, then everybody will do it. For the future of football, and a clean future, this kind of thing, if it happens, should be punished and not let people do something like that.

'I like natural money in football. For us, we will not have the budget of the top six or maybe top 10 teams in England, but we respect that.

'We have enough distance because of this income they have naturally. Please don’t add more distance. If there is a mistake like this, these kind of mistakes give crazy advantages to some teams and this is not fair.'

Despite news of the independent commission siding with the Premier League, Man City chief executive Ferran Soriano has warned their fight will still take ‘a lot more time’ to conclude.

Soriano was at a private meeting with the executive board of European Football Clubs’ body along with other bosses of top clubs and, according to sources, was quick to address the elephant in the room.

‘It’s taken eight years to get here,’ Soriano told the assembled club chiefs, ‘and it’s going to take a lot more time’.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said in a statement on Saturday: ‘The process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.’

City were found to have broken 114 of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League, having profited from an era of sustained success between 2009 and 2018

There has been a huge amount of discussion in the football community over potential sanctions for City, which could include expulsion and being stripped of their titles.

They lifted three Premier League titles as part of an eight-trophy haul during the years the charges cover.

JOE HART - I BELIEVE CITY ARE INNOCENT 'I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion. 'My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon. What he said is enough for me. 'I loved how he spoke. I loved the letterbecause that was from someone who cared about the club. 'If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there's conversations to be had. 'But right now I'm very confident and very, very calm. I'm very proud of what I've achieved and what I did with Man City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change. That doesn't change until you tell me. 'I did what I did. I lined up 11 v 11 and had it out on the pitch. I won some games, lost some games, drew some games, and I shook hands and I walked off. 'I know what I did, I know what we did, and I know how it happened. It didn't feel like we were scheming or plotting.'

Graeme Souness told Track Radio: 'If it goes the wrong way for them they’ll be consigned to history that they were cheats and whatever they did, whatever they won in that period, should not count.

'There’s an argument for Liverpool to have a couple of Premier Leagues given to them. For them [City] to be stripped of whatever they’ve won in that period of time, for them... money’s not an issue.'

Piers Morgan, speaking to Simon Jordan and Daily Mail Sport's Oliver Holt on Football Uncensored, said: 'They (Man City) 100 per cent have to be relegated. 100 per cent. This idea they get away with a fine and a transfer ban - no, no, no, no.

'I think they should be relegated, I think there should be a points deduction for the next four seasons. There's got to be a proper punishment. The fine is irrelevant, Abu Dhabi have gazillions pumping out of their oil barrels every day. It's got to hurt them.'

Holt, who urged in his Daily Mail column that City should be stripped of their titles as a deterrent, agreed with Morgan's suggested sanction – while Jordan insisted that the punishment cannot 'scorch' the Premier League.

The former Crystal Palace chairman also claimed that the guilty verdict should spell the end of the Abu Dhabi United Group's 'doomed' project at Manchester City.

But former City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart still believes in the club's innocence.

He told the BBC: 'I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion.

'My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon. What he said is enough for me.

'I loved how he spoke. I loved the letter because that was from someone who cared about the club.'

Hart added: 'If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there's conversations to be had.

'But right now I'm very confident and very, very calm. I'm very proud of what I've achieved and what I did with Manchester City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change. That doesn't change until you tell me.'

Sports.title: The Premier League's stars of the future: From Liverpool's Moneyball diamond and an £8m Man United project to an 'outrageous' Spurs talent and England youth captain at Newcastle, these are the 16 best wonderkids eyeing up top-flight debut
Sports.content:
The Premier League's stars of the future: From Liverpool's Moneyball diamond and an £8m Man United project to an 'outrageous' Spurs talent and England youth captain at Newcastle, these are the 16 best wonderkids eyeing up top-flight debut

JJ Gabriel is not the only talented teenager desperate for a Premier League debut.

Across the country, the stars of academy football are knocking on the door of the first team as they dream of realising their potential on the grandest stage.

Gabriel’s dispute with Manchester United, and the storm it created across the game, shows that youth players are big business these days. Liverpool took Rio Ngumoha from Chelsea and the 18-year-old is now in the full England squad. Once he has regular playing time, Arsenal’s 16-year-old attacking midfielder Max Dowman will not be far behind.

In partnership with prominent scouting platform Eyeball, and their football intelligence lead Alfred Frank, Daily Mail Sport has settled on the 16 most exciting youngsters yet to make their first appearances in England’s top flight.

Don't be surprised if this lot are soon following in the footsteps of Ngumoha and Dowman...

1. Brando Bailey-Joseph (Arsenal)

Age: 17, Position: Winger, Nation: England

The 17-year-old joined Arsenal aged eight and has become a skilful, pacy winger.

Bailey-Joseph’s speed on the left flank set him apart with Arsenal's Under 21s – for whom he featured regularly last season – and made the team far more potent on counter attacks.

The teenager struck nine goals and seven assists across all competitions last season and headed into this campaign full of confidence, having made his senior Arsenal debut in the Champions League in January against Kairat Almaty.

He recently suffered a major blow, sustaining an ACL injury in July which will see him on the sidelines for a significant period of time following surgery. A huge setback, yes, but one he can rebound from. Isaan Khan

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

Brando Bailey-Joseph struck nine goals and seven assists across all competitions last season and made his senior Arsenal debut in the Champions League in January against Kairat Almaty

2. Ceadach O'Neill (Arsenal)

Age: 18, Position: Central midfielder, Nation: Northern Ireland

The 18-year-old has quietly risen to prominence in the Arsenal youth set-up. His 18 goals in 30 appearances last season made him the academy’s top goalscorer, scored across three age levels.

It culminated in O’Neill being rewarded with his senior international debut, coming on for Northern Ireland in a 1-0 win over Guinea in June 2026.

O’Neill is one of Arsenal’s more intriguing young attackers because of his versatility and technical ability. Comfortable as a winger or an attacking midfielder, it’s his ability to beat defenders and play confidently in tight areas which makes him stand out.

The youngster courted a lot of interest from the Irish media in the mixed zone after Arsenal’s pre-season defeat by Real Betis in August.

He’s in the headlines at present amid a tug of war over who he will represent at international level, as he can still switch to the Republic of Ireland if he wishes. He pulled out of Northern Ireland’s latest squad to face Georgia on Friday with an injury. Isaan Khan

Ceadach O'Neill has quietly risen to prominence in Arsenal's academy, scoring 18 goals in 30 games last season across three age groups

3. TJ Carroll (Aston Villa)

Age: 19, Position: Centre back, Nation: England

Carroll is a ball-playing right-sided centre back who has been with Villa since the age of eight.

He featured during pre-season and trains regularly with the first team, including twice in the final week before the international break, in which Villa recorded two wins.

Following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal, Unai Emery decided to keep Carroll in the summer, rather than allowing him to leave on loan – though he may do so in January if first-team opportunities have not arrived by then.

He owes his impressive ability on the ball to his early days as a deep-lying midfield playmaker. Tom Collomosse

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

TJ Carroll owes his impressive ability on the ball to his early days as a deep-lying midfield playmaker

4. Reggie Watson (Chelsea)

Age: 16, Position: Central midfielder, Nation: England

You see Watson and think: ‘He’s 16? Really?'

He already carries a formidable frame, and yet he was the youngest player on Chelsea’s pre-season tour of Australia and Asia under Xabi Alonso, who was giving him personal advice about being a central midfielder.

He grew up in football as the son of former Premier League player and Wigan Athletic FA Cup hero Ben Watson, so knows what it takes to make it.

Given Chelsea's situation in midfield after failing to sign anyone on deadline day, some fans think this kid should be a substitute option already. He has continued to train with the first team here and there. He's on a promising pathway. Kieran Gill

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 4/5

You see Reggie Watson play and think: ‘He’s 16? Really?'

5. Braiden Graham (Everton)

Age: 18, Position: Forward, Nation: Northern Ireland

Everton’s threadbare squad may be bad news for David Moyes, but it’s good news for Graham.

Had things played out a little differently in the transfer window, the 18-year-old may well have headed out on loan to an EFL club. Instead, he is almost guaranteed to feature in most Premier League matchday squads given the Toffees' lack of attacking options.

Graham still has a boyish physique, but his ball-striking is excellent and he has been prolific at youth level. Former Leeds striker David Healy, Graham's manager at former club Linfield, was a key early influence. He received his first Northern Ireland call-up in June and was again named in Michael O'Neill's squad this international break.

A striker with Everton's Under 21s, Moyes sees Graham's future at first-team level in a different role given his lack of physical presence.

'I don’t think he’s a striker, first of all,' said Moyes recently. 'He’s probably someone who would play off the sides for us. I like Braiden, he’s trained with us quite a lot and he played in pre-season. He’s certainly moving in the right direction.' Alex Jennings

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 4/5

Braiden Graham still has a boyish physique, but his ball-striking is excellent and he has been prolific at youth level

6. Alfie Cresswell (Leeds United)

Age: 19, Position: Centre back/centre midfield, Nation: England

The younger brother of Charlie Cresswell, who is now with Rennes, Alfie is hugely admired by Leeds boss Daniel Farke and trains regularly with the first-team squad.

Farke believes Cresswell can operate on the right of a back three, using his natural ease in possession to step into midfield. For Leeds’ Under 21s side, Cresswell mostly operates in central midfield, as he did in the 4-3 win at Barnsley in the EFL Trophy on September 22.

Cresswell’s rapid progress suggests a senior debut is close, although breaking into any Premier League team is tough, especially one performing as consistently as Leeds at the moment. If he is made available for loan in January, though, there will be no shortage of takers in England and overseas. Tom Collomosse

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 4/5

Leeds head coach Daniel Farke believes Alfie Cresswell can operate on the right of a back three, using his natural ease in possession to step into midfield

7. Joshua Abe (Liverpool)

Age: 16, Position: Winger, Nation: England

The most talented kid in Liverpool’s academy and the best compliment he can be paid is to list the clubs that tried and failed to poach him this year: Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea, Real Madrid (and surely many more).

Liverpool tied him down, though, and Abe has already trained with the first team several times and featured on their pre-season tour. He is out injured at the moment with a shoulder issue that required minor surgery.

The winger has magic in his boots, can beat his man with ease and knows where the goal is. He is still very young, though, so patience must be advised but it would be a surprise if Abe does not break through. Lewis Steele

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

Joshua Abe has magic in his boots, can beat his man with ease and knows where the goal is

8. Mor Talla Ndiaye (Liverpool)

Age: 18, Position: Centre back, Nation: Senegal

This signing was one straight from Fenway Sports Group's Moneyball playbook, with Matt Newberry’s global talent team to thank for identifying Ndiaye.

The Reds scouted him playing for Senegal at the Under-17 World Cup and he arrived from Amitie FC, who are owned by former Premier League striker Demba Ba, for £1million.

Ndiaye is tall and left-footed, which gives him an advantage. He impressed in pre-season though fellow youngster Ifeanyi Ndukwe pushed ahead of him. He has been on the first-team bench a few times already. Lewis Steele

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

Liverpool scouted Mor Talla Ndiaye playing for Senegal at the Under-17 World Cup and he arrived from Amitie FC, who are owned by former Premier League striker Demba Ba

9. Will Wright (Liverpool)

Age: 18, Position: Striker, Nation: England

The 18-year-old was in talks with Arsenal throughout the summer of 2025 until Liverpool swept in at the last minute and poached him from Salford City, where he had made four first-team appearances.

It was a whirlwind weekend: he signed his contract on the Friday, passed his driving test on the Saturday and then played at Anfield in a friendly the next day.

His first year at the club saw him sidelined and needing surgery with a medial ligament injury. The striker is back now and played on the pre-season tour of America. He is a poacher with physicality beyond his years and fast when running in behind. Lewis Steele

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

Striker Will Wright is a poacher with physicality beyond his years and fast when running in behind

10. Floyd Samba (Manchester City)

Age: 17, Position: Central midfielder, Nation: England/Germany

The surname might feel familiar, with Samba the son of former Blackburn Rovers and Queens Park Rangers centre back Chris.

He has been in City’s youth set-up since he was a boy, having been scouted by City stalwart Mike Hayes at Wilmslow Football Academy and excelled throughout the age groups.

Samba has a surprising mentor in City's first-team squad. Despite his shy personality and the fact he has not yet mastered English, Abdukodir Khusanov has been one of the key figures in helping Samba make the step up, along with Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Khusanov will have been bursting with pride when Samba enjoyed a fantastic senior debut in a Carabao Cup clash with Norwich a few weeks ago.

The 17-year-old scored twice, saying: 'To get a debut like that is mind-blowing. The first-teamers have all been brilliant with me – before the game, giving me advice like, "Play your game, be you". Those words have given me confidence. This is just the beginning, I have got a big career ahead of me.'

Bold words. But you suspect Samba will back them up. Jack Gaughan

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 4/5

Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream Manchester City debut against Norwich this month, scoring twice

11. Amir Ibragimov (Manchester United)

Age: 18, Position: Forward, Nation: Russia

Deployed as a false nine as part of the Under 21s' shift towards mirroring the patterns of play of the first team, Ibragimov’s stocks are on the rise again this season.

The versatile Russian played as a deep-lying playmaker for Darren Fletcher’s Under 18s last season and is now the focal point of the Under 21s' attack.

Ibragimov has been a slow burn compared to many of his peers, who have been fast-tracked into the first-team training group, but those at United now believe the diminutive Russian is coming into his own.

‘There's obviously still loads more to come and to work on but he's definitely moving in the right direction and I think he's feeling quite confident and fit and strong at the moment, which is great,’ his Under 21s boss Adam Lawrence said recently. Nathan Salt

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

Versatile Russian Amir Ibragimov played as a deep-lying playmaker for Darren Fletcher’s Under 18s last season and is now the focal point of the Under 21s attack

12. Tynan Thompson (Manchester United)

Age: 18, Position: Winger, Nation: England

The latest Ineos project player, and one who will cost as much as £8million if he ends up realising the potential the likes of Jason Wilcox and Co see in him, having moved from Tottenham over the summer.

Thompson is yet to appear for the first team in a competitive match but has shown a real zip for the Under 21s, even without displaying the blistering pace that would propel him to a higher level in and of itself.

He doesn’t look first team ready just yet – physically he needs building up slowly – and is unlikely to get in ahead of Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo or Shea Lacey. But he is a player Ineos have invested time and money in – and they will want to see that recognised at the top level. Nathan Salt

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

13. Matheos Ferreira (Newcastle United)

Age: 18, Position: Winger, Nation: England/Italy/Brazil

He’s still just 18 but Ferreira has been around Newcastle since 2020 after joining the academy from Berwick Rangers. He has Italian and Brazilian heritage and that shows in his wing play.

He can play on either flank and is fast and direct – although his end product needs to improve. Until then, Matthias Jaissle is unlikely to call on him unless injuries force his hand. Craig Hope

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 2/5

14. Sam Alabi (Newcastle United)

Age: 17, Position: Midfielder, Nation: England

The 17-year-old midfielder joined from Oldham aged 14 in 2023, and it was regarded as something of a coup at the time.

He has since captained England at youth level and, last season, Eddie Howe named him on the bench several times after Alabi held his own in training with the seniors.

He is one Newcastle insiders talk about as having all the attributes to emerge as a first-team player. Craig Hope

Likelihood of PL debut this season: 3/5

Sam Alabi has captained England at youth level and, last season, Eddie Howe named him on the bench several times after the midfielder held his own in training with the seniors

15. Luca Williams-Barnett (Tottenham Hotspur)

Age: 17, Position: Midfielder/winger, Nation: England

An outrageously gifted attacking midfielder or winger who loves to run with the ball at his feet and has outstanding poise and balance. Williams-Barnett sees a pass, creates and scores, and is supremely confident in possession, some might say to the point of arrogance. He scored a Panenka penalty in a pre-season shootout against Sydney.

Signed from Luton at nine, he was in the Spurs first-team squad as soon as he turned 16, on the bench in a Champions League tie. He made his first senior appearance as a substitute in the Carabao Cup against Doncaster last season and came off the bench in the same competition last month against Charlton.

Roberto De Zerbi admitted he wanted to bring him on for a Premier League debut at Brentford on the opening day of this season but abandoned the plan because Spurs were 3-0 down and struggling. Matt Barlow

Age: 18, Position: Centre back, Nation: England

Centre back Hardy has been at Spurs since the age of eight. He is quick and strong, aggressive in the tackle and composed on the ball.

The 18-year-old is predominantly right-footed but can play on either side. He is 6ft 3in and good in the air in both boxes.

Often described as an old head on young shoulders, Hardy captained England through his age groups and forged a central defensive partnership for club and country with Jun’ai Byfield, who made his Premier League debut in February. He has even trained with Thomas Tuchel's senior group during this international break.

He has been in Tottenham's first-team squad on several occasions and he impressed De Zerbi during this summer’s pre-season tour Down Under. Hardy signed a new long-term deal at Spurs in April and made the permanent step up to the first-team squad this season. Matt Barlow

Sports.title: From 'repulsive' to indispensable: How Jude Bellingham has become central to Thomas Tuchel's plans... as under-pressure manager looks to England's 'real' deal to climb him out of a hole
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has been here before with England. In need of a step forward. Looking for a launchpad.

This time last year it came in Serbia as England travelled to Belgrade on the back of a mundane series of results and won 5-0 in World Cup qualifying.

Tuchel believes the few days spent training between a dull 2-0 home win over Andorra and their game in the Stadion Rajko Mitic were among the most crucial of his two years in office.

‘I felt something change and it was for the better,’ Tuchel has said.

All of that happened in the absence of Jude Bellingham. Back then – with Bellingham injured and Tuchel wrestling with issues of hierarchy within his squad – the England manager began to consider a future without the Real Madrid star as a regular starter.

As England landed in Prague on Monday looking to move on from Saturday’s defeat to Spain at Wembley, things have changed to a degree that it is now impossible to imagine a Tuchel team without Bellingham in it.

‘Jude looks like a real member of the squad on and off the pitch,’ said Tuchel last night.

Jude Bellingham has become central to Thomas Tuchel's England plans after a rocky start

The Real Madrid midfielder was immense during England's World Cup campaign last summer

‘The key in itself is that players want to come and want to really play and don't only say it but then prove the point when they are here.’

Such has been Bellingham’s transformation from enduring problem to the next England captain in waiting that even Tuchel’s language around him has changed.

It was as recently as early summer 2025 that Tuchel was describing some of the 23-year-old’s behaviour as ‘repulsive’ after a fractious defeat to Senegal at the City Ground in Nottingham.

Yet as he spoke in the Wembley interview area on Saturday night, he was comfortable enough to suggest Bellingham is at his best when playing with ‘rage’.

That reflects a softening of the relationship between player and coach. Bellingham still chooses to keep the majority of his thoughts on the matter to himself and that’s his prerogative.

Tuchel, though, has seen what he wanted to see from his most talented player around St George's Park and on England away trips. On the field, meanwhile, he has seen an improvement in the tactical and positional indiscipline that used to leave Tuchel forever concerned about just what Bellingham may do next.

‘I liked his performance a lot the other day because it was very consistent throughout the 90 minutes,’ he said.

‘It was a very mature, very good performance. He was always involved.

‘Jude can play in these high intensive patterns and then needs time to recharge the batteries.

‘But against Spain he had played economically and was always a difference maker, always available.’

England’s defeat by Spain at the weekend has left Tuchel under a little pressure. As such, he needs to look to players who can bring his team the consistency it now undeniably needs.

Missing the likes of Declan Rice in the centre of midfield and with his defence looking as unsure as any England back line has done for a long time, Tuchel’s England will need its big players to stand up in games against Czechia (home and away) and Croatia over the next eight days.

Having been England’s best player at the World Cup in America, Bellingham would appear to at last be feeding off the responsibility that comes with his status.

For a while it wasn’t the case. Too often his messages on the field of play were the wrong ones but it was noticeable on Saturday after captain Harry Kane slipped in missing a penalty that would have given his team a 3-1 lead, Bellingham was the first one on the scene to acknowledge exactly what had happened.

This is what Tuchel means when he talks about Bellingham looking like a ‘real member of the squad’. The 53-year-old knows that Bellingham will always present with rough edges. The task is to make sure it’s the opposition that takes the impact of them.

Tuchel has a big decision to make over whether to give Trent Alexander-Arnold his chance

The Three Lions are gearing up to face Czechia in the Nations League on Tuesday night

Asked if Bellingham himself had grown to love playing for his country, Tuchel said: ‘Yes and we also have to provide an environment and atmosphere where players can actually feel free and express themselves and be the best vision of themselves.

‘It is a give and go. We need to provide that and the player needs to have the hunger and the excitement to show up.’

England face a Czechia team short on form and results tonight but lost 2-1 here in 2019 and have some cleaning up to do after the nature of their defeat to Spain.

Tuchel knows what he saw when England had the ball at Wembley. England played with a purpose and belief that we didn’t often see during the summer’s World Cup and Bellingham – along with Barcelona’s Anthony Gordon - was at the heart of it.

Equally, England were a calamity waiting to happen in their own half and at the centre of the defence Tuchel only has inexperience in the shape of Jarrad Branthwaite and Trevoh Chalobah to call on as he looks to fix it.

Tuchel craves continuity with this England team. He has a spine of seven or eight players that he would pick every game if he could. Yet the fact he is missing a few and the nature of this September/October schedule means that he will have to mix and match a little in the days to come.

He was reluctant to yet again enter the Trent Alexander-Arnold debate, offering only two or three sentences when asked to explain his qualities. It feels as though that is one kind of background noise he could do without. The truth is, however, that Tuchel cannot rely on eleven players to take him where he wants to go ahead of the home Euros in 2028. He needs a core of sixteen or seventeen and maybe he is not quite there yet.

With his own country Germany losing to Greece this weekend under their new coach Jurgen Klopp, it was put to Tuchel that international management is maybe rather harder than people think.

‘Everyone told me that it is tough to form a team,’ nodded Tuchel.

Thomas Tuchel is under pressure after the World Cup and Saturday's defeat against Spain

‘There are so many ideas in football and everyone comes with different ones and the focus was, you know, to bring them together, play properly as a team and implement patterns of play. ‘And we are a step further. We had a tournament together, we had this experience together. We digested it.

‘We had a result that some think was not enough. Some think it was a good result. But we continue and this helps us.

‘It is a process. We are lacking a lot of players who have been with us from the World Cup, otherwise we would have been one more step ahead but I think you could see it was clear against Spain what we were trying to do.’

Expected England XI to face Czechia: (4-2-3-1) Trafford; Quansah, Guehi, Branthwaite, Hall; Anderson, Lewis Skelly; Rogers, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney insists he would NOT accept 2012 Premier League title if Man City are stripped of it and claims Man United do not 'deserve' to be awarded winners' medal - as legend opposes Rio Ferdinand and David De Gea's stance
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney insists he would NOT accept 2012 Premier League title if Man City are stripped of it and claims Man United do not 'deserve' to be awarded winners' medal - as legend opposes Rio Ferdinand and David De Gea's stance

Wayne Rooney has insisted Man United do not 'deserve' to be awarded the 2011-12 Premier League title and he would be 'uncomfortable' accepting a winners medal should Man City be stripped of the crown.

Rooney's former team-mates Rio Ferdinand and David De Gea have publicly called for the 2011-12 prize to be added to their medal collection, with City found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges made against them by the Premier League.

The bombshell verdict has opened a can of worms over how City's illustrious period from 2009-2018 should be judged, with players, fans and managers campaigning for the rewriting of history.

But United legend Rooney is adamant that Sir Alex Ferguson's class of 2011-12 are undeserving of the top prize, even if City are stripped of the title.

Wayne Rooney's United were denied at the Stadium of Light in 2012

Rio Ferdinand applauds the travelling United fans after the news of City's win comes through

'I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal... I wouldn't really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I'm being honest,' he said on Stick To United.

'I don't think we deserve it, we didn't do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away.'

'I've seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player's shoes... they're players, they're doing everything they can to try and win the Premier League title and in their mind they have done it, if those players have no understanding of what is going on above them, if that happened to me... I would be absolutely devastated.

'It might happen, they might take them [medals] away, but I wouldn't want it [a medal] because I don't think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn't finish first.

Sergio Aguero's late, late goal gave Manchester City their first title since 1968

'So when I see team-mates saying "I want a medal", I'm happy with the five I've won. I wouldn't want this one. Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn't feel comfortable accepting it.'

United suffered devastation on the final day having thought they had pulled off an unlikely title victory with a 1-0 win over Sunderland, secured by Rooney's header.

When the final whistle went at the Stadium of Light, City were surprisingly 2-1 down at home to QPR and needed a win to become champions with United having secured three points.

But just minutes later Edin Dzeko's equaliser was followed by Sergio Aguero's famous goal, snatching the title and leaving United stars heartbroken on the pitch.

Rooney's former United team-mates have also weighed in on the impending verdict, with David de Gea, who was also part of the team which missed out in 2012 and that which finished runners-up in 2017-2018 posting on X: 'So... Let's talk. How many Premier League titles have I won then?'

Rio Ferdinand, another member of the 2012 runners-up posted: 'Another premier league medal to be added to the cabinet.'

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel tells his England stars to stop being 'the biggest danger to ourselves' as they hunt for first clean sheet in seven following Spain errors
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has accused his England defence of being a danger to themselves.

They have not kept a clean sheet in six games since beating Panama at the World Cup, a run during which they have conceded 13 goals and leaked seven against Spain and France on their last two outings.

It might have been worse had Spain capitalised on a sequence of good early chances, mostly brought about by England's errors in possession, but Tuchel claimed to have no great concerns about the broader elements of defending.

Only that his team must kick the habit of self-destruction.

'We suffered from individual mistakes when we had the ball, especially in deep build-up,' said Tuchel, ahead of Tuesday's Nations League tie against the Czech Republic in Prague.

'It's something that we cannot repeat, especially not at this kind of level.

Thomas Tuchel has urged England to start taking more care in possession as they hunt a first clean sheet in seven games

The Three Lions shipped three against Spain on Sunday and will face Czechia on Tuesday

'To take care of this, we have to be technically absolutely clinical, under pressure. We need to improve these things. Strangely enough, when we had the ball, we were the biggest danger to ourselves around our box.

'But purely defending, no concerns. I trust we can do it. Some players of course are not here, who would also help organising our defensive block, I don't have any reason to be concerned.'

James Trafford will continue in goal in Prague, winning his fourth cap with Jordan Pickford set to return for games against Croatia on Saturday and the Czech return next week at Wembley.

Tuchel added: 'The last two matches, 6-4 against France and 2-3 v Spain, in itself seven goals in two matches is very unusual. I understand the question. I'm not concerned yet.

'I didn't see a pattern. We defended very well in a block when we were organized, but we had just big individual mistakes. But I could not see any defensive pattern that would concern me.

'I felt that we defended much more disciplined, cohesive and organised than in some matches in the World Cup. That was a step in the right direction. We constantly pushed out from our middle block, we tried to go into the opponent's half and pushed out of the deep block.

'We didn't suffer too for long periods of time in defending. We never lost our structure. So from all these things I'm not concerned. The result was heavily influenced by some individual mistakes that can happen, but the result was influenced but not the performance.'

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane becomes an instant meme with wild touchline celebration after Michael Olise's last-gasp winner for France in Belgium
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane becomes an instant meme with wild touchline celebration after Michael Olise's last-gasp winner for France in Belgium

New France manager Zinedine Zidane may have given up playing years ago, but rolled back the years on Monday as he celebrated his side's last-gasp winner over Belgium.

Zidane took over from Didier Deschamps after the World Cup, and has now won both of his matches in charge so far.

After overseeing a 1-0 win over Turkey in the Nations League on Friday, he guided his team to a victory in Belgium by the same score line on Monday.

It was Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise who netted the winning goal, with his strike coming in the 88th minute of the tense clash.

And Zidane wasn't hiding his emotion with his celebration as he sprinted down the touchline as soon as the ball hit the net.

The former midfielder then took it upon himself to boot a ball away in joy as one of the spare balls placed on a cone around the outside of the pitch went flying.

Allez, en haute définition, et avec la prise d'élan au complet! pic.twitter.com/7kgYOXw0jN — Saoirse Mulrane (@SaoirseMulrane) September 28, 2026

Zinedine Zidane caught the eye with his energetic celebration following France's win over Belgium on Monday

The France bench leapt up behind him, but there seemed to be no one happier than the 54-year-old.

Zidane, who won three Champions Leagues as Madrid manager, has signed a four-year deal with Les Bleus as he succeeds his former Juventus and France team-mate Deschamps.

Deschamps left his 14-year tenure as France manager at the end of the World Cup, with his side losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals. They finished fourth after a 6-4 defeat by England in the third-place play-off.

It is Zidane's first foray back into management since leaving Real Madrid in 2021, revealing he has rejected offers in the meantime as he waited for his 'dream' to become France boss.

'The French team was the only thing I wanted to do,' Zidane told reporters at his unveiling.

'I've always looked at this team through the eyes of a future manager. I didn't take a club job for that reason. The only thing I wanted to do after Madrid was manage the French national team.

The former midfielder has won both of his matches in charge since taking over this year

'I could have taken on a three-year role because Deschamps was there. He made that decision in January 2025, and the very next day I knew I wanted to be the next one. We met with the president and the deal was sealed.'

Deschamps oversaw 185 matches and 120 victories, guiding France to the 2018 World Cup title, the 2020-21 Nations League trophy, and the Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup finals.

He and Zidane share a long association, having also been team-mates in France's 1998 World Cup-winning side on home soil.

Zidane, who retired from playing in 2006, played a pivotal role in that triumph and won the Ballon d'Or that year. He made 108 appearances for the national side, scoring 31 goals and contributing 29 assists.

France have two matches remaining in the current international break. They will take on Italy on Friday, before the return match against Belgium next Monday.

Sports.title: England injury blow confirmed as Thomas Tuchel names squad for Czechia clash
Sports.content:
England injury blow confirmed as Thomas Tuchel names squad for Czechia clash

England will be without one of their starters from Saturday's 3-2 loss at home to Spain, forcing Thomas Tuchel to make a change to his starting line-up against Czechia

View 2 Images Nico O'Reilly won't feature in Prague (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

England star Nico O'Reilly has been ruled out of Tuesday's game against Czechia through injury - but Ezri Konsa is set to be available. Both players missed training on Monday ahead of flying to Prague for the Nations League encounter.

‌



O'Reilly, 21, played the entirety of England's 3-2 defeat at home to Spain on Saturday and remains Thomas Tuchel's first-choice left-back. But the Manchester City defender - who did make the journey - has been replaced in England's matchday squad by Liverpool forward Rio Ngumoha, who missed the clash with Spain.

‌



Konsa, on the other hand, has been included in Tuesday's squad and could keep his place at centre-back. The 28-year-old has been largely ever present under Tuchel, featuring in every game at the World Cup over the summer as well as for Arsenal since leaving Aston Villa in a deal worth up to £55million during the summer transfer window.

‌



Speaking in his pre-match press conference, Tuchel was unsure whether both Konsa and O'Reilly would be available to face Czechia. "It was because of minor issues," the England manager confirmed. "But there are still issues."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Speaking on Monday, Tuchel added: "Today in the morning we had a light training for the guys who started the game. The very last checks will be made tomorrow morning. If the doctors and physios give thumbs up then we’re good to go.

"One day longer would really make a difference. I feel the players who were on the pitch today all really want to play and are up for it."

Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham are expected to start, as the Three Lions bid to get their Nations League campaign up and running. Options to replace O'Reilly at left-back include Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

‌



How should England line up against Czechia? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa has been included in England's matchday squad (Image: Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Despite his side's need for victory, Tuchel has played down claims that it's a 'must-win' game. "It is a bit early in the group for 'must-win'," the German stated.

Article continues below

"We respect the quality of the opposition. I feel I always need a result, no matter where. Especially after defeat, even if this is the way to go forward, even then you just need it for yourself, and to show straight away a reaction. The match tomorrow has the highest priority."

England will next travel to Croatia for their third game this Saturday before hosting Czechia at Wembley next Tuesday.

Sports.content:
The latest news on Manchester City's charges after the club were found guilty of alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules

Welcome to our live blog on the latest Manchester City charges news, with the latest updates after the club were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules.

While the Premier League remain silent on the situation, City have spoken out a couple of times. The club's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has sent an open letter to fans and it has been reported that chief executive officer Ferran Soriano has suggested that the case is far from over in a meeting with senior figures from other Premier League clubs.

Sports.title: How Man Utd squad could look in 2027 as new contracts decided and five stars exit
Sports.content:
How Man Utd squad could look in 2027 as new contracts decided and five stars exit

Manchester United are set to face several dilemmas next year as manager Michael Carrick aims to prepare for the future

View 3 Images Manchester United manager Michael Carrick will face several key decisions next year (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Manchester United face several difficult decisions in 2027, with the squad in need of strengthening yet again. Michael Carrick will welcome players back from loan, decide on which stars deserve new deals and evaluate whether certain academy prospects are ready for first-team opportunities.

‌



United skipper Bruno Fernandes has entered the final 12 months of his current deal, which includes an option to extend by a further year. Fernandes is reportedly in talks over a fresh contract, which would make him the club's top earner, though there is speculation he could leave Old Trafford after six years.

‌



The Red Devils are set to make many more difficult calls next year as Carrick decides how to keep and who to sell from his current crop. Here's a closer look at the decisions set to shape United's 2027.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Expiring contract dilemmas

Centre-backs Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are two of the players whose contracts are set to end next summer, albeit both deals include an option to extend for a further year. United recently focused their recruitment efforts on midfield, but could look to shake up the defence in the near future.

Maguire has been a fixture of Carrick’s defence and brings vital experience to United’s squad. However, he will be 34 by the end of the season, and the club may choose to part ways rather than extend the England international’s deal, with the likes of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven already vying for a starting spot.

‌



Martinez is also an automatic pick when fit, but the Argentine has only once since signing in 2022 started more than 20 league games in a season. If he can play regularly, United could opt to trigger his extension, but another significant spell on the sidelines could put his future at United in doubt.

Moving to left-back, the problem position of the summer transfer window is set to rear its head again in 2027. Luke Shaw is in the final months of his contract and, unlike the aforementioned stars, does not have an option to extend for a further 12 months.

View 3 Images Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are two players who have entered the final year of their Manchester United contracts (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The experienced defender has been a regular in the side since overcoming his own fitness issues, but the 31-year-old is set for a demanding campaign after United failed to sign senior cover in his position. A contract extension would allow United to still benefit from his experience in the short term while also preventing the club from having to sign two new players in his position.

Young left-back Harry Amass is also nearing the end of his contract and continues to be on the fringes of the first team, despite a lack of recognised alternatives. The 19-year-old seeking regular football elsewhere may be the best way for his career to flourish, especially given the club’s recent pursuit of left-back targets.

‌



Midfielders Jack and Tyler Fletcher are also nearing the end of their deals, and the youngsters face fierce competition for places, though they could still make their mark before the end of the campaign. Meanwhile, veteran goalkeeper Tom Heaton is set to be out of contract and could hang up his boots at the end of the season, aged 41.

Returning loanees

The only senior players United currently have out on loan are goalkeepers Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir. Onana has returned for a second temporary spell at Trabzonspor, with the deal not including an option to buy, though he is unlikely to feature in United’s plans.

Bayindir has joined Celta Vigo, with the Spanish side able to make the goalkeeper’s stay permanent for £3.5million. Both shot-stoppers will have a year left on their United contracts at the end of their respective loan deals.

‌



View 3 Images Andre Onana is in his second loan spell with Trabzonspor (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images))

Youngsters Sekou Kone, Ethan Wheatley and Chido Obi are among the academy starlets who are hoping to send a message to Carrick during their time away from Old Trafford. The lack of orthodox strikers in United’s first team squad means that a prolific season for Obi or Wheatley could see them rise up the pecking order.

Academy starlets

While the JJ Gabriel saga rumbles on, United will be encouraged by several other academy starlets who could have their eyes on stepping up to the first team squad on a more regular basis. Shea Lacey has already scored his first senior goal for the club against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

‌



The 19-year-old winger will hopefully continue to grow in confidence and impress Carrick to cement his spot in the first team setup. Noah Ajayi is two years younger than Lacey but is another highly-rated prospect on the left flank, who recently signed his first professional deal.

United splashed out an initial £4m, plus another £4m in add-ons, for Tottenham Hotspur prospect Tynan Thompson. The 18-year-old will be eyeing up a battle with Marcus Rashford and Patrick Dorgu to be considered an option on the left wing.

Potential 2027/28 Man Utd squad as things stand…

Goalkeepers: Lammens, Darlow, Mee.

‌



Defenders: Martinez, Yoro, Heaven, De Ligt, Shaw, Diego Leon, Dalot, Mazraoui.

Midfielders: Baleba, Santos, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mount, Ugarte, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Fernandes.

Forwards: Rashford, Dorgu, Thompson, Amad, Lacey, Ajayi, Mbuemo, Cunha, Zirkzee, Sesko.

Sports.title: Man Utd 'arrange secret friendly' with Sir Jim Ratcliffe's other club who are bottom
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'arrange secret friendly' with Sir Jim Ratcliffe's other club who are bottom

Manchester United are looking to build some form and confidence during the international break after a dismal start to the season under Michael Carrick

View 2 Images None of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's clubs are enjoying strong seasons so far (Image: Bo Amstrup/Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images))

Manchester United will face Sir Jim Ratcliffe-owned Lausanne-Sport in a behind-closed-doors friendly during the international break. It has been a disappointing start to the 2026/27 season at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils have made their joint-worst start to a new campaign, equalling last term's dismal start under Ruben Amorim and the 1992/93 campaign under Sir Alex Ferguson. United's draw at Fulham last time out leaves Michael Carrick's men sitting 12th in the top-flight table.

‌



United now have several weeks to lick their wounds and regroup before returning to action at home to Tottenham Hotspur on October 10. And according to The Telegraph, United boss Carrick will get the opportunity to work on a few things in a secret friendly.

‌



The Red Devils will lock horns with minority owner Ratcliffe’s Swiss club Lausanne-Sport in the next few days. Details of the exact location, time and date of the game between Ratcliffe's teams are not yet known.

Man Utd injury blow confirmed as Patrick Dorgu immediately leaves Denmark camp READ MORE :

Lausanne could also use that friendly as they are dealing with an even worse season than the Premier League giants. The Swiss Super League side sit bottom of the table after losing five of their first nine matches.

Both struggling clubs under Ratcliffe have won just one league match so far this season. And they are not the only clubs owned by Ratcliffe, 73, who are desperate to improve their luck after the international break.

‌



The billionaire’s French outfit Nice are 14th in the Ligue 1 table with only two points separating them from the relegation zone. Olivier Pantaloni’s side have lost two of their first five matches.

United's women’s team under Ratcliffe are also struggling after tumbling down to ninth place in the Women's Super League table. Eva Olid’s side have lost half of their first four matches of which they also only won one.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick and Man Utd have arranged a friendly (Image: Javier Garcia/Shutterstock)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The poor start for United's men's side has included defeat at Hull City and a loss at home in the Manchester derby, albeit to an incorrectly awarded goal, despite playing against 10 men for much of that contest.

Problems were then compounded by a shambolic defeat at home to Brighton & Hove Albion in the League Cup. The collapse saw United lose after surrendering a two-goal lead at home.

‌



Carrick has downplayed concerns that United's poor start to the season is due to a lack of fitness in the squad. Matheus Cunha said Fulham's players "put in more energy" at the start of the second half of last Sunday's draw at Craven Cottage.

"It didn't look like that to me," Carrick said after being asked about Cunha's assessment. "I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. I thought we finished the game really strongly actually and we kept pushing. So I don't think that's an issue, no."
